ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r1.claim: A cited poem demonstrates that the person being concealed can be the direct object, followed by the thing concealed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r1.anchor: كتمتك ليلا بالجمومين ساهرا ... وهمين هما مستكنا وظاهرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r2.claim: The phrase أن يقول is causal, meaning because he says my Lord is God.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r3.claim: The believer is named Saman, Habib, or Hizqil; most read رجل with a damma, while Isa, Abd al-Warith, Ubayd ibn Aqil, and Hamza ibn al-Qasim read it with sukun, a Tamimi and Najdi form.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r3.anchor: قيل: واسمه سمعان. وقيل: حبيب. وقيل: حزقيل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r4.claim: Asking whether they will kill a man merely for saying his Lord is God is a forceful rebuke: their only basis for killing him is his truthful statement, despite proofs from their own Lord.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r4.anchor: وهذا إنكار منه عظيم وتبكيت لهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r5.claim: Saying the proofs came from your Lord, rather than only his Lord, subtly invites Pharaoh's people to acknowledge that Moses' God is theirs too.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari permits an omitted وقت before أن يقول, meaning they would kill Moses immediately upon hearing his words without reflection; Abu Hayyan rejects this because the required explicit verbal noun is absent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r6.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: ولك أن تقدر مضافا محذوفا، أي وقت أن يقول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p251/r7.claim: The proofs are evidence for monotheism, as in the debates with Pharaoh recorded in Ta Ha and al-Shu'ara'.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r1.claim: A poem says a careful person may attain part of a need while a hurried person may err, illustrating the rhetorical use of some.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r1.anchor: قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته ... وقد يكون مع المستعجل الزلل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the believer accepts Moses truth conditionally, then says some to understate its force and avoid appearing partisan.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وذلك أنه حين فرض صادقا، فقد أثبت أنه صادق في جميع ما يعد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari challenges the claim that some means all; Abu Hayyan cites al-Mazani rebuking that interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r3.anchor: فقد حق في قول المازني في مسألة العافي كان أحفى من أن يفقه ما أقول له

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r4.claim: Calling Moses an immoderate liar indirectly rejects the charge against him, since a prophet chosen by God cannot be such, while branding Pharaoh excessive in killing and false in claiming divinity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى علو شأن موسى، عليه السلام، وأن من اصطفاه الله للنبوة لا يمكن أن يقع منه إسراف ولا كذب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r5.claim: A hadith names three supremely truthful believers: Habib the carpenter of Yasin, the believer from Pharaoh's house, and Ali ibn Abi Talib.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r5.anchor: وفي الحديث: «الصديقون ثلاثة: حبيب النجار مؤمن آل يس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r6.claim: A hadith recounts Abu Bakr defending the Prophet at the Kaaba against Quraysh's threat, loudly repeating the believer's words with tears until they released him; Ja'far al-Sadiq says the believer spoke secretly while Abu Bakr spoke openly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r6.anchor: وعن جعفر الصادق: أن مؤمن آل فرعون قال ذلك سرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r7.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r7.claim: Al-Suddi interprets excess as excessive killing; Qatada interprets it as disbelief.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r7.anchor: وقال السدي: مسرف بالقتل. وقال قتادة: مسرف بالكفر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r8.speaker: صاحب التحرير والتحبير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r8.claim: The author of al-Tahrir wa-l-Tahbir calls the believer's subtle advocacy استدراج: he avoids naming Moses as a believer or prophet, begins with the audience's assumption that he may be lying, then implies the liar-description fits Pharaoh instead.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p252/r8.anchor: هذا نوع من أنواع علم البيان تسميه علماؤنا استدراج المخاطب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p253/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p253/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p253/r1.claim: The believer continues his tactful argument by first conceding the audience's view, then conditionally raising Moses' truth without appearing a partisan; his closing description indirectly characterizes Pharaoh as an excessive liar.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p253/r1.anchor: فإن الأنبياء لا تخل بشيء مما يقولونه

STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.claim: Verses 10–20 warn of the disbelievers’ Hereafter; this sets up the extended Moses and Pharaoh account, centered on a believer in Pharaoh’s House challenging opposition to Moses.
STUDYQURAN:40:intro/r8.anchor: Vv. 10–20 then tell of the place of the disbelievers in the Hereafter

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.claim: The Moses–Pharaoh account warns Quraysh, encourages Muhammad and his companions to endure trials until victory, and profiles a Pharaoh’s family believer as a lesson for Quraysh and hesitant sympathizers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p12/r5.anchor: A specific part of the account of Moses (sws) and the Pharaoh is recounted so that a reminder can be sounded

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.claim: The Moses and Pharaoh story supports the prior claim that a people rejecting their messenger are destroyed despite worldly grandeur, and assures the Prophet and companions to persevere in their duty.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p26/r2.anchor: when a messenger is sent to a nation and it denies him, then it is necessarily destroyed however much it may be superior

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r1.claim: The believer belonged to Pharaoh’s royal family, loved truth, and had sympathized with Moses’ reform before prophethood; after Moses killed a Copt, he warned Moses and urged his escape to Madyan.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r1.anchor: it was he who informed Moses (sws) about this intention and suggested to him to leave Egypt

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r2.claim: He embraced faith after Moses returned from Madyan but concealed it for a long time, apparently to serve Moses’ call more effectively from within Pharaoh’s House of Lords.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r2.anchor: for a considerable period of time, he hid his faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r3.claim: Had he declared faith earlier, Pharaoh could have publicly disgraced him as a national rebel and stripped him of his royal standing.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r3.anchor: the Pharaoh would have immediately made him a disgraced person before the whole nation by declaring him to be a national rebel

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r4.claim: Concealing faith for religious benefit may be permissible, but becomes hypocrisy once religion faces decisive danger; the believer spoke openly when Moses’ life was threatened.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r4.anchor: when he saw that Moses’ (sws) life was facing danger, he gave up this cautious behaviour

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r5.claim: The Qur’an’s account addresses Muhammad’s contemporaries: once opponents plot to kill him, believers may no longer hide their faith but should openly support him at risk to life.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p32/r5.anchor: now when their enemies are conniving with one another to kill Muḥammad (sws) it is not permissible for anyone to hide his faith

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r1.claim: The believer’s appeal that Moses said God was his Lord presents monotheism as an indisputable truth deserving support, not execution.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r1.anchor: to regard God as one’s Lord is an indisputable fact; if someone says so, he is expressing the radiant truth

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r2.claim: Moses’ clear signs prove he is God-sent; only the blind can refuse to recognize his mission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r2.anchor: The signs brought by Moses (sws) are a very clear proof of him being an envoy of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r3.claim: The believer reminds Pharaoh’s court that the Lord Moses represents is also their Lord; their error is treating others as lords beside Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r3.anchor: the Lord whose messenger he is declaring himself to be is also their messenger

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r4.claim: If Moses lies, the consequences fall on him; if he speaks truth, some threatened punishment will strike them, following God’s established treatment of rejecters and would-be killers of messengers.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r4.anchor: if he was lying in his claim to prophethood, then he will face its evil results and if he was true in this claim

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r5.claim: The conditional if he is lying reflects the audience’s supposed view, not genuine uncertainty; context and occasion determine whether a conditional conveys doubt.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r5.anchor: a doubt expressed in a conditional sentence is not always explicit in connoting doubt

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r6.claim: God does not guide here means He will not let a liar and transgressor succeed; this apparently wise principle also sarcastically targets Pharaoh in front of his court.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p33/r6.anchor: Here it is used to connote making a person succeed in his efforts

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r1.claim: After Moses responds to Pharaoh's plot only by seeking God's protection, God raises a separate person to defend him and calm the crisis.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r1.anchor: ما زاد في دفع مكر فرعون وشره على الاستعاذة بالله

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r2.claim: Razi says from personal experience that when he entrusts a wrongdoer's threatened harm to God without confronting him, God sends unknown people to oppose the harm vigorously.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r2.anchor: كلما قصدني شرير بشر ولم أتعرض له وأكتفي بتفويض ذلك الأمر إلى الله

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r3.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r3.claim: One reported identification says the believer was Pharaoh's cousin, effectively a crown prince and chief of police.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r3.anchor: فقيل إنه كان ابن عم لله ، وكان جاريا مجرى ولي العهد

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r4.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r4.claim: A second identification says he was a Copt among Pharaoh's people but not a relative.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r4.anchor: وقيل كان قبطيا من آل فرعون وما كان من أقاربه

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r5.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r5.claim: A third identification says he was an Israelite.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r5.anchor: وقيل إنه كان من بني إسرائيل

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r6.claim: Razi judges the first identification likelier because “āl” can mean kin and clan, citing the household of Lot in 54:34.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r6.anchor: والقول الأول أقرب لأن لفظ الآل يقع على القرابة والعشيرة

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r7.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r7.claim: A report from the Prophet names three foremost believers: Ḥabīb al-Najjār, the believer from Pharaoh's household, and ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, whom it calls the best of them; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r7.anchor: وعن رسول الله أنه قال : ( الصديقون ثلاثة : حبيب النجار

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r8.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r8.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad says Abū Bakr was better than the believer from Pharaoh's household: Abū Bakr proclaimed faith openly, while that believer concealed it.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r8.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد أنه قال : كان أبو بكر خيرا من مؤمن آل فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r9.claim: “Min” may modify “believer,” making the man a member of Pharaoh's household.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r9.anchor: لفظ من في قوله { من ءال فرعون } يجوز أن يكون متعلقا بقوله { مؤمن }

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r10.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r10.claim: A reported parse attaches “min” to “conceals his faith,” but an objection says Arabic does not express concealing something from someone in this construction; 4:42 is cited.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r10.anchor: وقيل إن هذا الاحتمال غير جائز لأنه يقال كتمت من فلان كذا

RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r11.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r11.claim: Most readers pronounce the jīm in “rajul” with ḍamma; another reading has kasra, as in the two pronunciations of ʿuḍud.
RAZI-FULL:v27p50/r11.anchor: المسألة الثالثة : رجل مؤمن الأكثرون قرأوا بضم الجيم

RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r1.claim: The question is an emphatic denial: the man has only said his Lord is God and brought signs, neither of which warrants killing.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r1.anchor: استفهام على سبيل الإنكار ، وقد ذكر في هذا الكلام ما يدل على حسن ذلك الاستنكار

RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r2.claim: The believer's phrase “my Lord is God” points to monotheism, while “clear proofs” refers to evidence for it, including Moses' statements in 20:50 and 26:24.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r2.anchor: قوله { ربى الله } إشارة إلى التوحيد

RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r3.claim: The believer offers a dilemma: if Moses lies, the burden of his lie is on him; if he is truthful, some promised punishment will reach them, so either way they should leave him alive.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r3.anchor: كان وبال كذبه عائدا علليه فاتركوه

RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r4.claim: An objection says a liar's harm would spread beyond himself because followers might adopt his false religion and provoke conflict.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r4.anchor: أنا لا نسلم أن بتقدير كونه كاذبا

RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r5.speaker: العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r5.claim: Razi says scholars unanimously hold that a heretic who calls people to his heresy should be killed.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r5.anchor: ولهذا السبب العلماء أجمعوا على أن الزنديق الذي يدعو الناس إلى زندقته يجب قتله

RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r6.claim: A second objection says that if this reasoning were sound, every liar could use it to defend a false religion.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r6.anchor: إن كان الكلام حجة له ، فلا كذاب إلا ويمكنه أن يتمسك بهذه الطريقة

RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r7.claim: A third objection says the reasoning would also forbid rejecting opponents of Moses: if their denial were false, its burden would be theirs, and if true, others could benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51/r7.anchor: وثالثها : أن الكفار الذين أنكروا نبوة موسى عليه السلام وجب أن لا يجوز الإنكار عليهم

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.claim: An objection asks why the believer says “some” of what Moses promises: soothsayers may partly predict events, but a prophet speaking revelation should be wholly truthful.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r1.anchor: كان من الواجب أن يقال وإن يك صادقا يصبكم كل الذي يعدكم لأن الذي يصيب في بعض ما يعد دون البعض هم أصحاب الكهانة والنجوم

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.claim: Razi answers the objections together: killing is unnecessary; they can stop Moses from publicly preaching and leave him alive, so a liar's harm stays with him while a truthful man's message can benefit them.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r2.anchor: لا حاجة بكم في دفع شره إلى قتله بل يكفيكم أن تمنعوه عن إظهار هذه المقالة

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r3.claim: “Some” is a fair minimum: if Moses lies, the harm is his; if he is truthful, at least some warning reaches them, which presents the case without obstinacy.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r3.anchor: مدار هذا الاستدلال على إظهار الإنصاف وترك اللجاج

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r4.claim: Moses threatened worldly and afterlife punishment; the arrival of worldly punishment would count as some of what he promised.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r4.anchor: كان يتوعدهم بعذاب الدنيا وبعذاب الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r5.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says “some” may mean “all,” citing Labīd's verse about death catching up with some souls.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r5.anchor: حكي عن أبي عبيدة أنه قال ورود لفظ البعض بمعنى الكل جائز

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r6.speaker: الجمهور
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r6.claim: The majority rejects Abū ʿUbayda's usage as mistaken, saying Labīd meant himself by “some souls.”
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r6.anchor: والجمهور على أن هذا القول خطأ ، قالوا وأراد لبيد ببعض النفوس نفسه

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r7.claim: The believer alludes that God guided Moses to manifest miracles, and one so guided cannot be a profligate liar; this indirectly exalts Moses and denies that he lies.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r7.anchor: ومن هداه الله إلى الإتيان بالمعجزات لا يكون مسرفا كذابا فهذا يدل على أن موسى عليه السلام ليس من الكاذبين

RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may describe Pharaoh as profligate in resolving to kill Moses and lying by claiming divinity; God will frustrate and destroy his power.
RAZI-FULL:v27p51#2/r8.anchor: أن فرعون مسرف في عزمة على قتل موسى

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r24.speaker: IJ, IK, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r24.claim: Many identify the believing man as Pharaoh’s cousin.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r24.anchor: Many propose that he was a cousin of Pharaoh (IJ, IK, Q, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r25.speaker: IJ, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r25.claim: Others say he was an Israelite, reading the phrase as a believer concealing his faith from Pharaoh’s family.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r25.anchor: Others say that he was an Israelite, in which case the meaning of this opening phrase is understood to be “a believing man who was concealing his belief from the family of Pharaoh” (IJ, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r26.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r26.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r26.claim: Al-Ṭabarī argues he was from Pharaoh’s family because a court outsider would not have been heard.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r26.anchor: Al-Ṭabarī argues that he was a man from Pharaoh’s family, since if he had been an Israelite or another person outside of Pharaoh’s court, no one in the court would have listened to him

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r27.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r27.claim: In either account, he is the man in 28:20 who ran to warn Moses that the notables plotted against him.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r27.anchor: In either interpretation, the believing man is the same person to whom reference is made in 28:20

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r28.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r28.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r28.claim: His protest resembles the sorcerers’ complaint after Pharaoh sentenced them for believing Moses; 5:59 and 85:9 condemn vengeance over belief.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r28.anchor: The question, Will you kill a man for saying, “My Lord is God”? is similar to the sorcerers’ complaint to Pharaoh

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r29.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r29.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r29.claim: The believer argues that truthful speech, especially backed by evidentiary miracles, cannot merit punishment.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r29.anchor: if Moses is truthful, he cannot be punished for speaking the truth, especially since he has brought clear proofs in the form of evidentiary miracles

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r30.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r30.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r30.claim: If Moses lies, he bears the consequences of his lie, so there is no need to punish him.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r30.anchor: if he is a liar, he will suffer the consequences of his lies; so there is no need to punish him

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r31.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r31.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r31.claim: Punishing Moses if he is truthful will bring even greater afflictions on his punishers.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r31.anchor: if he is punished for telling the truth, then even greater afflictions will befall those who punish him

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r32.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r32.speaker: Ṭ

STUDYQURAN:40:23/r33.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r33.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r33.claim: It can also mean one who transgresses God’s limits by lying about God.
STUDYQURAN:40:23/r33.anchor: or one who transgresses the limits set by God by lying about God (Ṭs)

TAB-FULL:v20p311/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r1.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r1.claim: Some say the man was one of Pharaoh’s people, had believed in Moses, and concealed his faith from Pharaoh and his people out of fear.
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r1.anchor: عن السدي، {وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون} [غافر: 28] قال: «هو ابن عم فرعون»

TAB-FULL:v20p311/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r2.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the concealed believer as Pharaoh’s cousin; the report also says he was the one who escaped with Moses.
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r2.anchor: عن السدي، {وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون} [غافر: 28] قال: «هو ابن عم فرعون»

TAB-FULL:v20p311/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r3.speaker: آخرون
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r3.claim: Another view holds that the man was an Israelite who concealed his faith from Pharaoh’s people.
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r3.anchor: وقال آخرون: بل كان الرجل إسرائيليا، ولكنه كان يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

TAB-FULL:v20p311/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r4.claim: If the phrase means he belonged to Pharaoh’s family, the reciter may pause after آل فرعون because the statement is complete there.
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r4.anchor: لأن ذلك خبر متناه قد تم

TAB-FULL:v20p311/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r5.claim: If he was an Israelite, the pause belongs after يكتم إيمانه, since من آل فرعون attaches to that clause.
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r5.anchor: والصواب على هذا القول لمن أراد الوقف أن يجعل وقفه على قوله: {يكتم إيمانه}

TAB-FULL:v20p311/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq is reported to identify the believer from Pharaoh’s family as Gabriel.
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r6.anchor: وقد ذكر أن " اسم هذا الرجل المؤمن من آل فرعون: جبريل " كذلك: حدثنا ابن حميد، قال: ثنا سلمة، عن ابن إسحاق

TAB-FULL:v20p311/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r7.claim: Al-Ṭabarī prefers that the man belonged to Pharaoh’s people: they listened to him and held back from killing Moses, whereas they would have punished an Israelite for intervening.
TAB-FULL:v20p311/r7.anchor: وأولى القولين في ذلك بالصواب عندي القول الذي قاله السدي من أن الرجل المؤمن كان من آل فرعون

TAB-FULL:v20p312/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r1.claim: The verse asks whether they would kill Moses for saying God is his Lord; the clear signs he brought demonstrate the truth of that claim. The clause أن is accusative.
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r1.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم} [غافر: 28] «بعصاه وبيده»

TAB-FULL:v20p312/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r2.claim: The clear proofs are signs demonstrating the truth of Moses’ claim, including his hand and staff.
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r2.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم} [غافر: 28] «بعصاه وبيده»

TAB-FULL:v20p312/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies the proofs as Moses’ staff and hand.
TAB-FULL:v20p312/r3.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، {وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم} [غافر: 28] «بعصاه وبيده»

TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r1.claim: The speaker sets out two outcomes: a lie is Moses’ burden, while truth brings punishment to them, so killing him only compounds God’s anger.
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r1.anchor: فلا حاجة بكم إلى قتله، فتزيدوا ربكم بذلك إلى سخطه عليكم بكفركم سخطا

TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r2.claim: An extravagant liar is one who transgresses by doing what he has no right to do and falsely attributes untruth to God.
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r2.anchor: يقول: إن الله لا يوفق للحق من هو متعد إلى فعل ما ليس له فعله، كذاب عليه يكذب، ويقول عليه الباطل وغير الحق

TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r3.claim: Qatadah glosses the extravagance as associating partners with God and thereby wronging oneself.
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، {إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب} [غافر: 28] «مشرك أسرف على نفسه بالشرك»

TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddi says the extravagant person is one who sheds blood unjustly, while also noting that the term is said of polytheists.
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي، {إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف كذاب} [غافر: 28] قال: " المسرف: هو صاحب الدم، ويقال: هم المشركون "

TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the wording broadly: both shirk and unjust bloodshed are extravagance, and Pharaoh combined both.
TAB-FULL:v20p312#2/r5.anchor: والشرك من الإسراف، وسفك الدم بغير حق من الإسراف، وقد كان مجتمعا في فرعون الأمران كلاهما

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r4.claim: When the plot to kill Moses spread, his friends grieved and his enemies rejoiced; God protected him and raised an outsider to calm the crisis and defend him.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r4.anchor: فلا جرم صانه الله من كل بلية وأوصله إلى كل أمنية

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r5.claim: مؤمن is the first of three descriptions of the man because it is noblest; من آل فرعون comes before يكتم إيمانه to prevent misreading it as the man’s relative clause.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r5.anchor: صفة ثالثة قدم الأول أعني مؤمن لكونه أشرف الأوصاف

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r6.claim: A person’s آل are those whose affairs return to him through kinship, companionship, or agreement in religion.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r6.anchor: وآل الرجل خاصته الذين يؤول إليه أمرهم للقرابة

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r7.claim: The believer was a relative, specifically a cousin, of Pharaoh and the same person who had warned Moses of the plot in 28:20; Bursevī considers Shamaʿān the soundest reported name.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r7.anchor: وكان ذلك الرجل المؤمن من أقارب فرعون

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r8.speaker: الإمام السهيلي
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r8.claim: Al-Suhaylī identifies the believer as Shamaʿān and Bursevī calls this the soundest view.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r8.anchor: وهو أصح ما قيل فيه. قاله الإمام السهيلي

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r9.speaker: الطبري
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r9.claim: Al-Ṭabarī’s History gives the believer’s name as Jabr.

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r10.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r10.claim: Another identification is Ḥabīb al-Najjār, said to have made the chest in which Moses’s mother placed him in the river; he is distinguished from the man of Yā Sīn.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r10.anchor: وهو الذي عمل تابوت موسى حين أرادت أمه أن تلقيه

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r11.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r11.claim: Other reported names for the believer are Khirbil ibn Nūḥāʾīl and Ḥizqīl.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r11.anchor: وقيل : خربيل بن نوحائيل أو حزقيل

BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r12.speaker: النبي
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r12.claim: A Prophetic report counts Ḥizqīl, the believer among Pharaoh’s people, Ḥabīb al-Najjār of Yā Sīn, and ʿAlī as three who never disbelieved; it says ʿAlī is best among them.
BURSEVI:v8p132#3/r12.anchor: قوله عليه السلام سباق الأمم ثلاثة لم يكفروا بالله طرفة عين

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r9.claim: The context makes “from Pharaoh’s household” and “concealing his faith” two descriptions: he is a Copt in Pharaoh’s inner circle, whose faith they do not know.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r9.anchor: ظاهر السياق أن { من آل فرعون } صفة رجل و { يكتم إيمانه } صفة اخرى

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r10.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r10.claim: A reported parse makes “from Pharaoh’s household” the second object of “conceals,” placed before the verb.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r10.anchor: وقيل قوله { من آل فرعون } مفعول ثان لقوله { يكتم } قدم عليه

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r11.speaker: المصباح
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r11.claim: Al-Miṣbāḥ allows the second object of “conceals” to take min, though the usual construction is direct.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r11.anchor: لكنه قد يتعدى إليه بمن كما صرح به في المصباح

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r12.claim: Tabatabai rejects the alternative: context gives no clear reason to front the second object, such as restriction.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r12.anchor: وفيه أن السياق يأباه فلا نكتة ظاهرة تقتضي تقدم المفعول الثاني على الفعل من حصر ونحوه

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r13.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r13.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r13.claim: His repeated address to Pharaoh and his people as “my people” confirms that he belonged to them.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r13.anchor: على أن الرجل يكرر نداء فرعون وقومه بلفظة { يا قوم } ولو لم يكن منهم لم يكن له ذلك

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r14.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r14.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r14.claim: The question condemns their plan to kill Moses; the signs establish that God is their Lord too, so Moses brought them truth from their Lord.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r14.anchor: وفي قوله { من ربكم } دليل على أن في البينات التي جاء بها دلالة على أن الله ربهم أيضا

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r15.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r15.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r15.claim: One view takes the falsehood condition as tactful argument, not evidence that the believer doubted Moses’ truthfulness.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r15.anchor: قيل إن ذكره هذا التقدير تلطف منه لا أنه كان شاكا في صدقه

TABATABAI:40:26-28/r16.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r16.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r16.claim: The believer argues from the least threatening case: even part of the promised punishment suffices, although Moses’ truth entails all of it.
TABATABAI:40:26-28/r16.anchor: فيه تنزيل في المخاصمة بالاكتفاء على أيسر التقادير وأقلها كأنه يقول وإن يك صادقا يصبكم ما وعدكم

TABATABAI:40:28-33/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r1.claim: The clause explains only the truthful-Moses case: the people then transgress by denying their Lord and taking other lords.
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r1.anchor: تعليل للتقدير الثاني فقط والمعنى إن يك كاذبا كفاه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم لأنكم حينئذ مسرفون

TABATABAI:40:28-33/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r2.claim: If Moses lies, his lie is enough to condemn him; the supposed lord he follows has no real lordship relevant to guidance.
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r2.anchor: وأما على تقدير كذبه فلا ربوبية لمن اتخذه ربا حتى يهديه أو لا يهديه

TABATABAI:40:28-33/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r3.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r3.claim: Some attach the clause to both conditions; Tabatabai rejects this because it does not fit the false-Moses case.
TABATABAI:40:28-33/r3.anchor: ما ذكره بعضهم من كون الجملة تعليلا للتقديرين جميعا متعلقة بكلتا الجملتين غير مستقيم

TABATABAI:40:21-54/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r2.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r2.claim: In al-Majmaʿ, Imam al-Ṣādiq says taqiyya is his and his fathers’ religion, indispensable to religion and God’s shield on earth; the believer would have been killed had he disclosed Islam.
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله التقية ديني ودين آبائي

TABATABAI:40:21-54/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r3.claim: Tabatabai says Shia reports on taqiyya are numerous and cites Qur’anic allowances for fearing hostile people and for a coerced believer.
TABATABAI:40:21-54/r3.anchor: والروايات من طرق الشيعة فيها كثيرة والآيات تؤيدها

TABRISI:40:26-28/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:26-28/r16.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:40:26-28/r16.claim: Abū ʿAbd Allāh says dissimulation is part of his and his forefathers' religion, and one who has no dissimulation has no religion.
TABRISI:40:26-28/r16.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله ع: التقية من ديني ودين آبائي ولا دين لمن لا تقية له

TABRISI:40:28-29/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:28-29/r1.claim: Dissimulation is God's shield on earth, because the believing man from Pharaoh's family would have been killed had he openly declared Islam.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r1.anchor: والتقية ترس الله في الأرض لأن مؤمن آل فرعون لو أظهر الإسلام لقتل

TABRISI:40:28-29/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:40:28-29/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the only other believers in Pharaoh's family were Pharaoh's wife and the believer who warned Moses that the council planned to kill him.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لم يكن من آل فرعون مؤمن غيره وغير امرأة فرعون

TABRISI:40:28-29/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r3.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
TABRISI:40:28-29/r3.claim: Al-Suddī and Muqātil say he was Pharaoh's cousin who believed in Moses and was the man who came running from the farthest part of the city.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r3.anchor: قال السدي ومقاتل كان ابن عم فرعون وكان آمن بموسى وهو الذي جاء من أقصى المدينة يسعى

TABRISI:40:28-29/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:28-29/r4.claim: Another view says he was Pharaoh's designated successor and was named Ḥabīb.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r4.anchor: وقيل: إنه كان ولي عهده من بعده وكان اسمه حبيب

TABRISI:40:28-29/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:28-29/r5.claim: A separate report gives his name as Ḥizbīl.

TABRISI:40:28-29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:28-29/r6.claim: The question rebukes them; using a participle meaning a man who says my Lord is God would not show that belief is the reason for killing him.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r6.anchor: وهو استفهام إنكار ولو قال أتقتلون رجلا قائلا ربي الله لم يدل على أن القتل من أجل الإيمان

TABRISI:40:28-29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:28-29/r7.claim: The subjunctive أن يقول is a causal object, meaning they would kill him because he says that his Lord is God.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r7.anchor: فموضع أن يقول نصب على أنه مفعول له

TABRISI:40:28-29/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:28-29/r8.claim: The clear proofs of Moses' truth include the staff, the hand, and other miracles.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r8.anchor: أي بما يدل على صدقه من المعجزات مثل العصا واليد وغيرهما

TABRISI:40:28-29/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:28-29/r9.claim: The believer softens his argument by saying that if Moses lies, the consequence falls on him, like the diplomatic wording in 34:24.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r9.anchor: إنما قال هذا على وجه التلطف كقوله

TABRISI:40:28-29/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r10.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:28-29/r10.claim: One explanation says Moses promised rescue for belief and destruction for disbelief; whichever course they chose, one of his promised outcomes would reach them.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r10.anchor: قيل: إن موسى كان يعدهم بالنجاة إن آمنوا وبالهلاك إن كفروا

TABRISI:40:28-29/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r11.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:28-29/r11.claim: Another explanation says his warnings included different events, such as destruction in this world and punishment in the next; earthly destruction is part of the warning.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r11.anchor: وقيل: إنما قال { بعض الذي يعدكم } لأنه توعدهم أمورا مختلفة

TABRISI:40:28-29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:40:28-29/r12.claim: Some can idiomatically mean all as a tactful or expansive expression; the cited poem says the patient may attain some of his wish while the hasty may err.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r12.anchor: وقيل: استعمل البعض في موضع الكل تلطفا في الخطاب وتوسعا في الكلام كما قال الشاعر: قد يدرك

TABRISI:40:28-29/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r13.speaker: علي بن عيسى
TABRISI:40:28-29/r13.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā says the believer argues that even part of Moses' warning suffices to destroy them, so the whole warning is more than enough.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r13.anchor: وقال علي بن عيسى: إنما قال بعض الذي يعدكم على المظاهرة بالحجاج أي أنه يكفي بعضه

TABRISI:40:28-29/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:28-29/r14.claim: The statement means God does not guide to Paradise and reward someone excessive in sin and lying about God.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r14.anchor: أي لا يهدي إلى جنته وثوابه من هو مسرف على نفسه متجاوز عن الحد في المعصية

TABRISI:40:28-29/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:40:28-29/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:40:28-29/r15.claim: The sentence may continue the believer's words, or it may begin a new statement from God.
TABRISI:40:28-29/r15.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون هذا حكاية عن قول المؤمن ويجوز أن يكون ابتداء الكلام من الله تعالى

THALABI:v8p272/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r11.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v8p272/r11.claim: One view says the believing man belonged to Pharaoh's household, believed in Moses, and hid his faith from Pharaoh and his people out of fear.
THALABI:v8p272/r11.anchor: فقال بعضهم: كان من آل فرعون، غير أنه كان آمن بموسى، وكان يكتم إيمانه من فرعون وقومه خوفا على نفسه.

THALABI:v8p272/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r12.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
THALABI:v8p272/r12.claim: Al-Suddi and Muqatil say he was Pharaoh's cousin and the man described as coming from the far side of the city to Moses.
THALABI:v8p272/r12.anchor: قال السدي ومقاتل: كان ابن عم فرعون

THALABI:v8p272/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r13.speaker: آخرون
THALABI:v8p272/r13.claim: Others say he was an Israelite and construe the phrase as a believer who concealed his faith from Pharaoh's people.
THALABI:v8p272/r13.anchor: وقال آخرون: كان إسرائيليا، ومجاز الآية: وقال رجل مؤمن يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون.

THALABI:v8p272/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p272/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر العلماء
THALABI:v8p272/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas and most scholars give the believer's name as Hizbil.
THALABI:v8p272/r14.anchor: فقال ابن عباس وأكثر العلماء: اسمه حزبيل.

THALABI:v8p273/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r1.speaker: وهب بن منبه
THALABI:v8p273/r1.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says the believer's name was Huzayqal.

THALABI:v8p273/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
THALABI:v8p273/r2.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives his name as Khirbil.

THALABI:v8p273/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
THALABI:v8p273/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq reports that the man who believed in Pharaoh's household was named Habib.

THALABI:v8p273/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p273/r4.claim: In that he says, an means because: they would be killing a man because he says, My Lord is God.
THALABI:v8p273/r4.anchor: أتقتلون رجلا أن أي لأن يقول ربي الله

THALABI:v8p273/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r5.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
THALABI:v8p273/r5.claim: Some scholars of meaning say some of what he promises intends all of it; Arabic can use some to mean all.
THALABI:v8p273/r5.anchor: وقال بعض أهل المعاني: أراد يصبكم كل الذي يعدكم. والعرب تذكر البعض وتريد الكل،

THALABI:v8p273/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r6.speaker: لبيد
THALABI:v8p273/r6.claim: Labid's line uses some souls to mean all souls, as evidence for the idiom.
THALABI:v8p273/r6.anchor:
كقول لبيد:
تراك أمكنة إذا لم أرضها … أو يرتبط بعض النفوس حمامها

THALABI:v8p273/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p273/r7.claim: The verse characterizes the person who exceeds bounds as an associator and a liar against God.
THALABI:v8p273/r7.anchor: إن الله لا يهدي من هو مسرف مشرك.

THALABI:v8p273/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r8.speaker: السدي
THALABI:v8p273/r8.claim: Al-Suddi glosses musrif as a killer.
THALABI:v8p273/r8.anchor: وقال السدي: قتال. كذاب على الله.

THALABI:v8p273/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v8p273/r9.claim: Kadhdhab here means someone who lies about God.

THALABI:v8p273/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v8p273/r10.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
THALABI:v8p273/r10.claim: Amr ibn al-As recounts Quraysh seizing the Prophet's garment after his circumambulation and challenging his preaching; Abu Bakr embraced him from behind, cited this verse in tears, and Quraysh released him.
THALABI:v8p273/r10.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص قال: ما تؤول من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيء كان أشد من أن طاف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r6.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r6.claim: An unassigned reported interpretation takes “some of what he promises” to mean all that he promises.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:40:25-29/r6.anchor: يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم } قيل: كل الذي يعدكم

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r1.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r1.claim: Some took the believing man from Pharaoh’s family to be an Israelite, a view Elmalılı does not accept as the phrase’s apparent sense.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r1.anchor: bazıları bu zâtın İsrâilîlerden olduğunu zannetmişlerse de

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r2.claim: The apparent meaning of being from Pharaoh’s household points instead to an Egyptian, perhaps a member of Pharaoh’s own dynasty.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r2.anchor: vasfının zâhiri bunun daha ziyade Mısırlılardan ve belki Firavun’un kendi hânedânından olduğunu anlatıyor

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r3.speaker: Süddî
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r3.claim: Al-Suddī relates that the believer was Pharaoh’s cousin.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r3.anchor: Süddî bunu Firavun’un amcası oğlu diye rivayet eylemiştir

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r4.claim: Another reported identification makes the believer heir apparent and head of the police.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r4.anchor: Veliyy-i ahdi ve sâhib-şurtası, yani polis nâzırı olduğu da söylenmiştir

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r5.claim: Because God especially recounts this man’s speeches and struggle against Pharaoh and his family, the sūra is named Sūrat al-Muʾmin after him.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r5.anchor: bu sûreye onun nâmına muzâf olarak “Sûre-i Mü’min” denilmiştir

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r6.claim: He concealed his faith and used secret stratagems to keep Pharaoh at bay for a time; when Moses’ execution was decided, he came forward, beginning with gradual counsel and then open opposition.

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r7.claim: At first he speaks cautiously without revealing his faith, arguing from the injustice of killing a man for saying that his Lord is God and from the proofs Moses had brought.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r7.anchor: Bir adamı “Rabbim Allah” diyor diye öldürecek misiniz?

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r8.claim: If Moses is lying, the lie and its consequence fall on him, so there is no need to kill him before his falsehood is established.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r8.anchor: Binâen‘aleyh yalancılığı tahakkuk etmeden öldürmeye ihtiyâcınız yok

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r9.claim: If Moses is truthful, at least some of his threatened punishment will befall them, even in this world if they reject the afterlife.

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r10.claim: One inference is that if Moses were an extreme liar, God would not have given him clear signs or supported him with miracles.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r10.anchor: o aşırı bir yalancı olsa idi Allah ona o beyyineleri vermez, o mucizelerle teyid eylemezdi

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r11.claim: The other inference is that a truly profligate liar would not succeed, so there is no need to strive to kill him.

ELMALILI:40:28-35/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r12.claim: Both arguments indirectly target Pharaoh: as a blood-shedding profligate liar, God will not help him kill Moses, and Pharaoh will only bring harm on himself.
ELMALILI:40:28-35/r12.anchor: asıl maksad da Firavun’a târizdir. Yani sen bu kadar kan döken müsrif bir yalancısın

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r1.claim: Zamakhshari and Razi report that the believer from Pharaoh’s family was Pharaoh’s cousin and of Coptic origin.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r1.anchor: Firavun’un amcasının oğlu, Kıptî asıllı biri olduğu rivayet edilir (Zemahşerî, III, 368; Râzî, XXVII, 58).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r2.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur says the unnamed believer was probably a virtuous, thoughtful man searching for religious truth who recognized it in Moses’ call, believed, and intervened to dissuade Pharaoh; Pharaoh heeded his advice because he belonged to his own people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r2.anchor: İbn Âşûr’a göre ismi bilinmeyen bu kişi muhtemelen dinî arayışı olan, bu hususta düşünüp taşınan aklı selim sahibi ve erdemli biriydi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r3.speaker: İbn Âşûr
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur identifies this believer with the person alluded to in Exodus 10:7, where Pharaoh’s servants urge him to release the Israelites to worship God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r3.anchor: İbn Âşûr, Tevrat’ın Çıkış kitabında (10/7) geçen, “Ve Firavun’un kulları kendisine dönüp dediler: Ne vakte kadar bu adam bize tuzak olacak?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r4.claim: When Uqba ibn Abi Muayt attacked and tried to strangle Muhammad at the Kaaba, Abu Bakr grabbed and rescued him, then repeated this verse’s words about killing a man for saying his Lord is God and bringing proofs; Bukhari and Musnad report it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r4.anchor: Ukbe b. Ebû Muayt isimli putperestin, Kâbe’de bulunan Hz. Peygamber’e saldırarak boğazına sarıldığını gören Hz. Ebû Bekir, saldırganı ellerinden yakalayarak Resûllah’ı kurtarmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r5.claim: Ali is reported to have said that Abu Bakr’s act was more significant than the believer’s because the believer hid his faith, whereas Abu Bakr declared his and committed his property and life to the cause.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r5.anchor: Hz. Ali’nin, “Allah’a yemin ederim ki Ebû Bekir’in davranışı Firavun ailesinden olan mümin kişininkinden daha da önemlidir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r6.claim: The believer’s conditional wording does not imply doubt about Moses; it was a tactic to prevent a rash execution and get Pharaoh’s people to consider the message calmly before deciding.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r6.anchor: Mûsâ’nın ortaya koyduğu gerçekler hakkında kuşkusu olduğu anlamına gelmez. Bu ifadesiyle o, Firavun ve taraftarlarının fevrî davranarak Mûsâ’yı öldürmelerini önlemeyi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r7.claim: The passage gives a general lesson to respond to different beliefs with restraint and clear-headedness, think through their truth or falsehood, and only then decide how to act.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r7.anchor: farklı bir düşünce ve inanç ortaya koyanlar karşısında ölçülü, soğukkanlı davranmak, sağ duyuyla hareket etmek; bunların doğruluğu ve yanlışlığı üzerinde düşünüp taşındıktan sonra bir karara varmak

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r9.claim: Pharaoh’s claim that he only shows what he sees suggests the believer’s words seemed justified to others, or at least raised doubts about whether killing Moses was right.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:40:28/r9.anchor: Firavun’un, “Ben sadece kendi gördüğümü size gösteriyorum ve sizi yalnızca doğru yola yönlendiriyorum” şeklindeki ifadesinden, mümin kişinin söylediklerinin başkaları tarafından haklı görüldüğü

BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r1.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r1.claim: After Abū Bakr died, Medina erupted in grief like it had at the Prophet's death; ʿAlī came weeping and said the caliphate of prophethood had ended.
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r1.anchor: قال لما قبض أبو بكر رضي الله عنه ارتجت المدينة بالبكاء كيوم قبض النبي

BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r2.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r2.claim: In his eulogy, ʿAlī praised Abū Bakr as the first Muslim, strongest in faith and certainty, most God-fearing, and foremost in service to Islam and the Messenger.
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r2.anchor: كنت أول القوم إسلاما وأخلصهم إيمانا وأشدهم يقينا وأخوفهم لله

BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r3.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r3.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r3.claim: ʿAlī said Abū Bakr affirmed the Messenger when others rejected him, and that revelation named him among those who brought truth and believed it.
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r3.anchor: صدقت رسول الله حين كذبه الناس فسماك في تنزيله صديقا

BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r4.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r4.speaker: علي
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r4.claim: ʿAlī praised Abū Bakr's companionship in hardship and the cave, his succession to the Messenger, and his steadfast leadership when others faltered after the Prophet's death.
BAQILLANI:v1p143#2/r4.anchor: ثاني اثنين وصاحبه في الغار والمنزل عليه السكينة والوقار ورفيقه في الهجرة وخليفته في دين الله

BURHAN:v4p63/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.claim: The author urges attention to these verses' arrangement as part of the Qur'an's inimitability, which must be contemplated.
BURHAN:v4p63/r1.anchor: فالتفت إلى تنزيل الكلام في الآيتين يلح لك ما اشرت إليه في هذا فان التدبر لاعجاز القرآن واجب مفترض

BURHAN:v4p63/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p63/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p63/r4.claim: The believer from Pharaoh's family uses the same tactic, letting the opponent enter through its less threatening possibility.
BURHAN:v4p63/r4.anchor: وكذا قوله تعالى عن مؤمن آل فرعون ﴿ وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم ﴾

BURHAN:v2p442/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p442/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p442/r6.claim: The examples place nominal material, a prepositional phrase, and a verbal clause in sequence; the adverbial form belongs between them because it resembles both noun and clause.
BURHAN:v2p442/r6.anchor: ﴿ وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه ﴾

BURHAN:v3p233/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p233/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p233/r2.claim: Placing من آل فرعون before يكتم إيمانه makes clear that the believing man belongs to Pharaoh's people; delaying it would obscure that meaning.
BURHAN:v3p233/r2.anchor: فإنه لو أخر قوله ﴿ من آل فرعون ﴾ فلا يفهم أنه منهم

BURHAN:v1p269/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p269/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p269/r2.claim: Al-Ma’ida is also called al-ʿUqud and al-Munqitha; Ghafir is also al-Tawl and al-Mu’min, the latter name drawn from “a believing man.”
BURHAN:v1p269/r2.anchor: وكسورة غافر والطول والمؤمن لقوله ﴿ وقال رجل مؤمن ﴾

BURHAN:v3p271/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p271/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p271/r2.claim: The description with a single adjective precedes the clausal description: “believing” comes before the clause “concealing his faith.”
BURHAN:v3p271/r2.anchor: ومنه تقديم الوصف بالمفرد على الوصف بالجملة في قوله ﴿ وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون يكتم إيمانه

BURHAN:v2p346/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p346/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p346/r4.claim: Al-Zarkashi says this contradicts the rhetoricians’ consensus: the cited questions refer to past actions; no evidence supports future reference, and the grammar of أتقتلون does not determine the intended time.
BURHAN:v2p346/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي قاله مخالف لاجماع البيانيين ولادليل فيما ذكره بل الاستفهام في الآيتين عن ماض

BURHAN:v2p346/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p346/r5.speaker: ابن جني
BURHAN:v2p346/r5.claim: Ibn Jinni notes that grammatical inflection can differ from the meaning; the future-subjunctive أن in “that he says” does not make the condemnatory question’s event future in sense.
BURHAN:v2p346/r5.anchor: وقد ذكر ابن جني في التنبيه ( 3 ) أن الإعراب قد يرد خلاف ما عليه المعنى

BURHAN:v2p264/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p264/r9.speaker: ثعلب
BURHAN:v2p264/r9.claim: Tha‘lab says some of the warning means the worldly punishment, one part of a threat that also includes punishment in the afterlife; it does not deny the latter.
BURHAN:v2p264/r9.anchor: فقال ثعلب انه كان وعدهم بشيء من العذاب عذاب الدنيا وعذاب الآخرة

BURHAN:v2p264/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p264/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p264/r10.claim: The author says Tha‘lab misread the cited poem: its “some souls” means the speaker himself, one soul among many, and the line means he never returns to a place he has left.
BURHAN:v2p264/r10.anchor: الثاني انه اخطأ في فهم البيت وإنما مراد الشاعر ببعض النفوس نفسه هو

BURHAN:v2p268/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p268/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v2p268/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari recounts, with a caveat about the report’s authenticity, Abu Ubayda’s exchange with al-Mazani over whether the alif in عَلْقَى marks femininity or is an added letter; Ru’bah’s verse and its singular form prompted the dispute.
BURHAN:v2p268/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري ان صحت الرواية عن أبي عبيدة فيدخل فيه قول المازني في مسألة العلقي

BURHAN:v2p268/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p268/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p268/r2.claim: People may accept that an entire threat is not carried out, so they have still less reason to object to only part of it; the sura’s later promise to show only part before death supports Tha‘lab’s reading.
BURHAN:v2p268/r2.anchor: ان الوعيد مما لايستنكر ترك جميعه فكيف بعضه ويدل قوله في آخر هذه السورة

SULAMI:v2p209#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p209#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p209#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ contrasts believers, who love and defend one another and offer counsel, with hypocrites, who posture for one another and object.
SULAMI:v2p209#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : المؤمن يألف المؤمن ويذب عنه والمنافق يراءى المنافق . ويجادل عنه والمؤمن ينصح والمنافق يعترض

ITQAN:v3p99/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r3.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ITQAN:v3p99/r3.claim: Abu Ubayda takes some in these phrases to mean all.
ITQAN:v3p99/r3.anchor: والثاني إطلاق لفظ بعض مرادا به الكل ذكره أبو عبيدة وخرج عليه قوله

ITQAN:v3p99/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r5.speaker: ثعلب
ITQAN:v3p99/r5.claim: Thaʿlab reads some literally: the threatened worldly punishment may befall them as one part of the threat, without excluding punishment in the afterlife.
ITQAN:v3p99/r5.anchor: ( يصبكم هذا العذاب في الدنيا وهو بعض الوعيد من غير نفي عذاب الآخرة ) ذكره ثعلب

ITQAN:v3p99/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r6.speaker: الزركشي
ITQAN:v3p99/r6.claim: Al-Zarkashi supports the literal partial-threat reading: an entire threat may be left unfulfilled, so its partial fulfillment is unproblematic; 40:77 offers a parallel.
ITQAN:v3p99/r6.anchor: قال الزوكشي ويحتمل أيضا أن يقال إن الوعيد مما لا يستنكر ترك جميعه فكيف بعضه

ITQAN:v3p99/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r7.claim: A specific noun can stand for a general referent: messenger is singular in the example but means the messengers of the Lord of the worlds.
ITQAN:v3p99/r7.anchor: الخامس إطلاق إسم الخاص على العام نحو ﴿ إنا رسول رب العالمين ﴾ أي رسله

ITQAN:v3p99/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r8.claim: A general expression can refer specifically to believers: those in the earth whom angels ask forgiveness for are identified as the believers.
ITQAN:v3p99/r8.anchor: السادس عكسه نحو ﴿ ويستغفرون لمن في الأرض ﴾ أي المؤمنين بدليل قوله

ITQAN:v3p99/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r9.claim: The text names a further figure of speech: using the name of a prerequisite for what necessarily follows from it.
ITQAN:v3p99/r9.anchor: السابع إطلاق إسم الملزوم على اللازم نحو

ITQAN:v3p99/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r10.claim: The reverse figure uses a necessary condition to mean the action it entails: asking whether God can give a table means asking whether He will do so.
ITQAN:v3p99/r10.anchor: الثامن عكسه نحو ﴿ هل يستطيع ربك أن ينزل علينا مائدة من السماء ﴾ أي هل يفعل

ITQAN:v3p99/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r11.claim: A result may name its cause: provision and clothing are used for rain, which produces them.
ITQAN:v3p99/r11.anchor: أي مطرا يتسبب عنه الرزق واللباس

ITQAN:v3p99/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r12.claim: In the phrase about those who cannot find marriage, marriage means the funds and necessities needed to marry.
ITQAN:v3p99/r12.anchor: أي مؤنة من مهر ونفقة وما لا بد للمتزوج منه

ITQAN:v3p99/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p99/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p99/r13.claim: A cause may be named for its result: inability to hear means inability to accept and act on what was heard.
ITQAN:v3p99/r13.anchor: العاشر عكسه نحو ﴿ ما كانوا يستطيعون السمع ﴾ أي القبول والعمل به

ITQAN:v3p203/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r1.speaker: الحذاق من النحاة وأهل البيان
ITQAN:v3p203/r1.claim: Skilled grammarians and rhetoricians hold that speech has only two kinds, report and composition, with no third category.
ITQAN:v3p203/r1.anchor: الحذاق من النحاة وغيرهم وأهل البيان قاطبة على انحصار الكلام فيهما وأنه ليس له قسم ثالث

ITQAN:v3p203/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r2.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v3p203/r2.claim: One proposed taxonomy has ten kinds: calling, questioning, command, intercession, exclamation, oath, condition, assertion, doubt, and interrogation.
ITQAN:v3p203/r2.anchor: وادعى قوم أن أقسام الكلام عشرة نداء ومسألة وأمر وتشفع وتعجب وقسم وشرط ووضع وشك واستفهام

ITQAN:v3p203/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r3.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r3.claim: A nine-kind taxonomy drops interrogation because it is included within questioning.
ITQAN:v3p203/r3.anchor: وقيل تسعة بإسقاط الاستفهام لدخوله في المسألة

ITQAN:v3p203/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r4.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r4.claim: An eight-kind taxonomy drops intercession because it is included within questioning.
ITQAN:v3p203/r4.anchor: وقيل ثمانية بإسقاط التشفع لدخوله فيها

ITQAN:v3p203/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r5.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r5.claim: A seven-kind taxonomy drops doubt because it belongs to the category of report.
ITQAN:v3p203/r5.anchor: وقيل سبعة بإسقاط الشك لأنه من قسم الخبر

ITQAN:v3p203/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r6.speaker: الأخفش
ITQAN:v3p203/r6.claim: Al-Akhfash divides speech into six kinds: report, inquiry, command, prohibition, calling, and wishing.
ITQAN:v3p203/r6.anchor: وقال الأخفش هي ستة خبر واستخبار ولأمر ونهي ونداء وتمن

ITQAN:v3p203/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ITQAN:v3p203/r7.claim: Another classification has five kinds: report, command, explicit declaration, request, and calling.
ITQAN:v3p203/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم خمسة خبر وأمر وتصريح وطلب ونداء

ITQAN:v3p203/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r8.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v3p203/r8.claim: Another classification has four kinds: report, inquiry, request, and calling.
ITQAN:v3p203/r8.anchor: وقال قوم أربعة خبر واستخبار وطلب ونداء

ITQAN:v3p203/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r9.speaker: كثيرون
ITQAN:v3p203/r9.claim: Many scholars divide speech into report, request, and composition: report can be judged true or false, while the other two cannot.
ITQAN:v3p203/r9.anchor: وقال كثيرون ثلاثة خبر وطلب وإنشاء قالوا لأن الكلام إما أن يحتمل التصديق والتكذيب أو لا

ITQAN:v3p203/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r10.speaker: المحققون
ITQAN:v3p203/r10.claim: The authoritative scholars include request within composition: the request to strike coincides with the word, while the later striking is only its requested object.
ITQAN:v3p203/r10.anchor: والمحققون على دخول الطلب في الإنشاء

ITQAN:v3p203/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r11.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r11.claim: Some say report cannot be defined because its nature is difficult to capture.
ITQAN:v3p203/r11.anchor: وقد اختلف الناس في حد الخبر فقيل لا يحد لعسره

ITQAN:v3p203/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r12.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r12.claim: Others say report is self-evident because people necessarily distinguish it from composition; the Imam in al-Mahsul prefers this view.
ITQAN:v3p203/r12.anchor: وقيل لأنه ضروري لأن الإنسان يفرق بين الإنشاء والخبر ضرورة ورجحه الإمام في المحصول

ITQAN:v3p203/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r13.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر والمعتزلة
ITQAN:v3p203/r13.claim: Al-Qadi Abu Bakr and the Muʿtazilites define report as speech admitting truth or falsehood; against the objection of God's report, al-Qadi says language permits either possibility.
ITQAN:v3p203/r13.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر والمعتزلة الخبر الكلام الذي يدخله الصدق والكذب

ITQAN:v3p203/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r14.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r14.claim: Another definition calls report speech that admits affirmation or denial, avoiding the objection raised against the prior definition.
ITQAN:v3p203/r14.anchor: وقيل الذي يدخله التصديق والتكذيب وهو سالم من الإيراد المذكور

ITQAN:v3p203/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r15.speaker: أبو الحسن البصري
ITQAN:v3p203/r15.claim: Abu al-Hasan al-Basri defines report as speech that itself conveys a relation; the definition is challenged because a command also relates an action to its subject.
ITQAN:v3p203/r15.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن البصري كلام يفيد بنفسه نسبة

ITQAN:v3p203/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r16.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r16.claim: One alternative defines report as speech that itself positively or negatively relates one matter to another.
ITQAN:v3p203/r16.anchor: وقيل الكلام المفيد بنفسه إضافة أمر من الأمور إلى أمر من الأمور نفيا أو إثباتا

ITQAN:v3p203/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r17.speaker: قائلون
ITQAN:v3p203/r17.claim: Another definition describes report as an utterance explicitly affirming or denying a relation between known things.
ITQAN:v3p203/r17.anchor: وقيل القول المقتضي بصريحه نسبة معلوم إلى معلوم بالنفي والإثبات

ITQAN:v3p203/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p203/r18.speaker: المتأخرون
ITQAN:v3p203/r18.claim: Later scholars define composition as speech that brings its meaning into external existence, with report defined by contrast.
ITQAN:v3p203/r18.anchor: وقال المتأخرين الإنشاء ما يحصل مدلوله في الخارج بالكلام والخبر خلافه

ITQAN:v1p153/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r1.speaker: السخاوي
ITQAN:v1p153/r1.claim: Al-Sakhawi says Surat Ta-Ha is also called Surat al-Taklim.
ITQAN:v1p153/r1.anchor: طه تسمى أيضا سورة التكليم ذكره السخاوي في جمال القراء

ITQAN:v1p153/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r2.claim: Surat al-Shuʿara is also called al-Jamiʿa in Malik's tafsir.
ITQAN:v1p153/r2.anchor: الشعراء وقع في تفسير الإمام مالك تسميتها بسورة الجامعة

ITQAN:v1p153/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r3.claim: Surat al-Naml is also called Surat Sulayman.

ITQAN:v1p153/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r4.claim: Surat al-Sajda is also called al-Madajiʿ.

ITQAN:v1p153/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r5.claim: Surat Fatir is also called Surat al-Malaʾika.

ITQAN:v1p153/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r6.speaker: النبي ﷺ
ITQAN:v1p153/r6.claim: The Prophet called Surat Ya-Sin the heart of the Qur'an; al-Tirmidhi transmits this from Anas.
ITQAN:v1p153/r6.anchor: يس سماها صلى الله عليه وسلم قلب القرآن أخرجه الترمذي من حديث أنس

ITQAN:v1p153/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r7.speaker: أبو بكر
ITQAN:v1p153/r7.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits a marfuʿ report from Abu Bakr calling Ya-Sin al-Muʿimma, al-Dafiʿa, and al-Qadiya, with promised worldly and next-worldly good, protection from evil, and fulfillment of needs; al-Bayhaqi calls it munkar.
ITQAN:v1p153/r7.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي من حديث أبي بكر مرفوعا سورة يس تدعى في التوراة المعمة نعم بخيري الدنيا والآخرة

ITQAN:v1p153/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r8.claim: Surat al-Zumar is also called Surat al-Ghuraf.

ITQAN:v1p153/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r9.claim: Surat Ghafir is called al-Tawl and al-Muʾmin; the latter title comes from the phrase about a believing man in 40:28.
ITQAN:v1p153/r9.anchor: غافر تسمى سورة الطول والمؤمن لقوله تعالى فيها

ITQAN:v1p153/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r10.claim: Surat Fussilat is also called al-Sajda and Surat al-Masabih.

ITQAN:v1p153/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r11.speaker: الكرماني
ITQAN:v1p153/r11.claim: Al-Karmani records al-Shariʿa and Surat al-Dahr as names for Surat al-Jathiya.
ITQAN:v1p153/r11.anchor: الجاثية تسمى الشريعة وسورة الدهر حكاه الكرماني في العجائب

ITQAN:v1p153/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r12.claim: Surat Muhammad is also called Surat al-Qital.

ITQAN:v1p153/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r13.claim: Surat Qaf is also called Surat al-Basiqat.

ITQAN:v1p153/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r14.claim: The sura beginning Iqtarabat is also called Surat al-Qamar.

ITQAN:v1p153/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r15.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p153/r15.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits a report from Ibn Abbas calling al-Qamar al-Mubayyida, which whitens its reciter's face on the day faces turn black; al-Bayhaqi grades it munkar.
ITQAN:v1p153/r15.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي عن ابن عباس أنها تدعى في التوراة المبيضة تبيض وجه صاحبها يوم تسود الوجوه

ITQAN:v1p153/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r16.speaker: علي
ITQAN:v1p153/r16.claim: Al-Bayhaqi transmits a marfuʿ report from Ali calling al-Rahman the Bride of the Qur'an.
ITQAN:v1p153/r16.anchor: الرحمن سميت في حديث عروس القرآن أخرجه البيهقي عن علي مرفوعا

ITQAN:v1p153/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r17.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r17.claim: In Ubayy ibn Kaʿb's codex, Surat al-Mujadila is called al-Zihar.
ITQAN:v1p153/r17.anchor: المجادلة سميت في مصحف أبي الظهار

ITQAN:v1p153/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p153/r18.claim: When Saʿid ibn Jubayr called it Surat al-Hashr, Ibn Abbas said to call it Surat Bani al-Nadir instead.
ITQAN:v1p153/r18.anchor: أخرج البخاري عن سعيد بن جبير قال قلت لابن عباس سورة الحشر قال قل سورة بني النضير

ITQAN:v1p153/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r19.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p153/r19.claim: Ibn Hajar says Ibn Abbas may have disliked al-Hashr because readers could mistake it for the Day of Judgment, whereas the name here means the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir.
ITQAN:v1p153/r19.anchor: قال ابن حجر كأنه كره تسميتها بالحشر لئلا يظن أن المراد يوم القيامة وإنما المراد به هنا إخراج بني النضير

ITQAN:v1p153/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r20.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p153/r20.claim: Ibn Hajar says the common vocalization al-Mumtahana has fatḥa and describes the woman on whose account the sura was revealed; with kasra it describes the sura itself.
ITQAN:v1p153/r20.anchor: قال ابن حجر المشهور في هذه التسمية أنها بفتح الحاء وقد تكسر فعلى الأول هو صفة المرأة التي نزلت السورة بسببها وعلى الثاني هي صفة السورة

ITQAN:v1p153/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r21.speaker: جمال القراء
ITQAN:v1p153/r21.claim: Jamal al-Qurra also records al-Imtihan and al-Mawadda as names for Surat al-Mumtahana.
ITQAN:v1p153/r21.anchor: وفي جمال القراء تسمى أيضا سورة الإمتحان وسورة المودة

ITQAN:v1p153/r22.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r22.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p153/r22.claim: Surat al-Saff is also called Surat al-Hawariyyin.

ITQAN:v1p153/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r23.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p153/r23.claim: Al-Bukhari and others transmit Ibn Masʿud's name for Surat al-Talaq, al-Nisa al-Qusra.
ITQAN:v1p153/r23.anchor: الطلاق تسمى سورة النساء القصرى كذا سماها ابن مسعود أخرجه البخاري وغيره

ITQAN:v1p153/r24.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p153/r24.speaker: الداودي وابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p153/r24.claim: Al-Dawudi objects that al-Qusra is not reliably preserved, but Ibn Hajar says this rejects established reports without evidence; qasr and tul are relative, as Zayd ibn Thabit calls al-Aʿraf one of the two longest suras.
ITQAN:v1p153/r24.anchor: وقد أنكره الداودي فقال لا أرى قوله القصرى محفوظا ولا يقال في سورة من القرآن قصرى ولا صغرى

ITQAN:v1p133/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r1.speaker: أبو هريرة
ITQAN:v1p133/r1.claim: Ahmad transmits from Abu Hurayra that the seven revealed forms include the synonymous descriptions knowing, wise, forgiving, and merciful.
ITQAN:v1p133/r1.anchor: وعند أحمد من حديث أبي هريرة أنزل القرآن على سبعة آحرف عليما حكيما غفورا رحيما

ITQAN:v1p133/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r2.speaker: عمر
ITQAN:v1p133/r2.claim: Ahmad transmits from Umar that Qur'anic variants are all sound unless they turn forgiveness into punishment or punishment into forgiveness; al-Suyuti calls the chains good.
ITQAN:v1p133/r2.anchor: وعنده أيضا من حديث عمر أن القرآن كله صواب ما لم تجعل مغفرة عذابا أو عذابا مغفرة أسانيدها جياد

ITQAN:v1p133/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r3.speaker: ابن عبد البر
ITQAN:v1p133/r3.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr says the seven forms may differ in wording while sharing an understood meaning, with no form contradicting or negating another.
ITQAN:v1p133/r3.anchor: قال ابن عبد البر إنما أراد بهذا ضرب المثل للحروف التي نزل القرآن عليها إنها معان متفق مفهومها مختلف مسموعها

ITQAN:v1p133/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ITQAN:v1p133/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb is reported to read 2:20 with alternatives meaning they passed through it or hurried through it, illustrating equivalent wording variants.
ITQAN:v1p133/r4.anchor: ثم أسند عن أبي بن كعب أنه كان يقرأ

ITQAN:v1p133/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p133/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud is reported to read 57:13 with alternatives meaning give us time or delay us.
ITQAN:v1p133/r5.anchor: وكان ابن مسعود يقرأ ﴿ للذين آمنوا انظرونا ﴾ أمهلونا أخرونا

ITQAN:v1p133/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r6.speaker: الطحاوي
ITQAN:v1p133/r6.claim: Al-Tahawi says the seven forms were a concession for people who struggled with one fixed wording because literacy, writing, and precise memorization were difficult; the concession was abrogated when those obstacles passed.
ITQAN:v1p133/r6.anchor: قال الطحاوي وإنما كان ذلك رخصة لما كان يتعسر على كثير منهم التلاوة بلفظ واحد لعدم علمهم بالكتابة والضبط وإتقان الحفظ ثم نسخ بزوال العذر

ITQAN:v1p133/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r7.speaker: ابن عبد البر والباقلاني وآخرون
ITQAN:v1p133/r7.claim: Ibn Abd al-Barr, al-Baqillani, and others likewise hold that the seven-form concession ended once its cause was removed.
ITQAN:v1p133/r7.anchor: وكذا قال ابن عبد البر والباقلاني وآخرون

ITQAN:v1p133/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v1p133/r8.claim: A report through Awn ibn Abd Allah says Ibn Masʿud taught a man who could not pronounce al-athim to recite al-fajir instead, illustrating accommodation in recitation.
ITQAN:v1p133/r8.anchor: وفي فضائل أبي عبيد من طريق عون بن عبد الله أن ابن مسعود أقرأ رجلا

ITQAN:v1p133/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r9.speaker: أبو عبيد وثعلب والأزهري وآخرون
ITQAN:v1p133/r9.claim: A tenth view, adopted by Abu Ubayd, Thaʿlab, al-Azhari, and others, understands the seven forms as seven Arabic languages; Ibn Atiyya preferred it and al-Bayhaqi authenticated it in al-Shuʿab.
ITQAN:v1p133/r9.anchor: القول العاشر إن المراد سبع لغات وإلى هذا ذهب أبو عبيد وثعلب والأزهري وآخرون واختاره ابن عطية وصححه البيهقي في الشعب

ITQAN:v1p133/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r10.speaker: المعترضون
ITQAN:v1p133/r10.claim: Critics object that Arab dialects number more than seven; proponents answer that the seven means the most eloquent dialects.
ITQAN:v1p133/r10.anchor: وتعقب بأن لغات العرب أكثر من سبعة وأجيب بأن المراد أفصحها

ITQAN:v1p133/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p133/r11.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas identifies five of the seven languages with the Hawazin clans Saʿd, Jusham, Nasr, and Thaqif, collectively called the upper Hawazin; Abu Amr says they and lower Tamim were the most eloquent Arabs.
ITQAN:v1p133/r11.anchor: فجاء عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس قال نزل القرآن على سبع لغات منها خمس بلغة العجز من هوازن

ITQAN:v1p133/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p133/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p133/r12.claim: Another route from Ibn Abbas says the Qur'an came in the language of the two Kaʿbs, Quraysh and Khuzaʿa, whose neighboring communities shared a familiar language.
