ITQAN:v1p133/r12.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد من وجه آخر عن ابن عباس قال نزل القرآن بلغة الكعبيين كعب قريش وكعب خزاعة

ITQAN:v4p426/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p426/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p426/r1.claim: In a report from al-Shaʿbi, Umar asks a traveling group for the greatest Qur'anic verse and Ibn Masʿud answers the Throne Verse, 2:255.
ITQAN:v4p426/r1.anchor: أخرج السلفي في المختار من الطيوريات عن الشعبي قال لقي عمر بن الخطاب ركبا في سفر فيهم ابن مسعود فأمر رجلا

ITQAN:v4p426/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p426/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p426/r2.claim: Asked which verse is most wise, Ibn Masʿud answers 16:90, God's command to justice, excellence, and giving to kin.
ITQAN:v4p426/r2.anchor: قال نادهم أي القرآن أحكم فقال ابن مسعود

ITQAN:v4p426/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p426/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p426/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud names 99:7–8, the atom's-weight verses, as the most comprehensive verse.
ITQAN:v4p426/r3.anchor: قال نادهم أي القرآن أجمع فقال

ITQAN:v4p426/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p426/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p426/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud identifies 4:123, whoever does evil will be repaid for it, as the saddest verse.
ITQAN:v4p426/r4.anchor: قال نادهم أي القرآن أحزن فقال

ITQAN:v4p426/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p426/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
ITQAN:v4p426/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud calls 39:53, the prohibition on despairing of God's mercy, the most hopeful verse.
ITQAN:v4p426/r5.anchor: قال نادهم أي القرآن أرجى فقال

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r1.claim: The polished-sword comparison defends gray hair by focusing on its white color, as a polished blade is more beautiful than an unpolished one.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r1.anchor: والصارم المصقول أحسن حالة يوم الوغى من صارم لم يصقل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r2.claim: That conceit deliberately ignores the other associations that make people dislike and criticize gray hair.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r2.anchor: وقد ترك أن يفكر فيما عدا ذلك من المعاني التي يكره لها الشيب ويناط بها العيب

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r3.claim: Poetry and oratory may treat two coincident features as a cause even when reason does not establish the causal premise; the audience accepts the premise for the conceit.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r3.anchor: أن يجعلوا اجتماع الشيئين في وصف علة الحكم يريدونه وإن لم يكن في المعقول ومقتضيات العقول

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r4.claim: Jurjani cites al-Buhturi’s complaint that poets are being required to follow the limits of logic, saying poetry’s imaginative falsehood can stand in place of proof.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r4.anchor: كلفتمونا حدود منطقكم في الشعر يكفي عن صدقة كذبه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r5.claim: Jurjani takes al-Buhturi to mean imaginative poetic reasoning, not knowingly attributing undeserved virtues to a patron, which would be exposed by examining the person.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r5.anchor: إذ يبعد أن يريد بالكذب إعطاء الممدوح حظا من الفضل والسؤدد ليس له

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r6.claim: The maxim “best poetry is the most false” means that poetry uses imaginative reversals, such as making the miser generous or the coward lionlike, not factual slander or praise.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r6.anchor: فكم جواد بخله الشعر وبخيل سخاه وشجاع وسمه بالجبن وجبان ساوى به الليث

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r7.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r7.claim: Poetry’s artistry is assessed in its own diction and workmanship, not by whether its invented character descriptions are literally true.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p234/r7.anchor: ثم لم يعتبر ذلك في الشعر نفسه حيث تنتقد دنانيره وتنشر ديابيجه ويفتق مسكة فيضوع أريجه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r1.claim: “Ask the village” means ask its inhabitants, since inanimate matter cannot be questioned; the verse is not meant literally.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r1.anchor: لأجل علمه أن الجماد لا يسأل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r2.claim: Imagining that God gave the village life so it could answer would not be unbelief, but it would be a claim the speaker knows to be false.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r2.anchor: لو تجاهل متجاهل فادعى أن الله تعالى خلق الحياة في تلك القرية حتى عقلت السؤال وأجابت عنه ونطقت لم يكن قال قولا يكفر به

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r3.claim: A reader must not cling to a literal surface that risks ruin or falling into associationism when the context requires figurative meaning.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r3.anchor: فمن حقه أن لا يجثم ههنا على الظاهر ولا يضرب الحجاب دون سمعه وبصره

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r4.claim: Jurjani rejects forced interpretations that ignore whether the wording can bear them, displace a clear benefit, and pursue obscure readings for display or deception.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r4.anchor: احتمال اللفظ شرط في كل ما يعدل به عن الظاهر فهم يستكرهون الألفاظ على الأمثلة من المعاني

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r5.speaker: رسول الله
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r5.claim: The Prophet says upright people in every generation carry this knowledge and clear away distortions, fabrications, and ignorant interpretations.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r5.anchor: قال رسول الله يحمل هذا العلم من كل خلف عدو له ينفون عنه تحريف الغالين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r6.claim: True carrying of knowledge means understanding its meanings, sources, paths, and methods, not merely transmitting its wording.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p340/r6.anchor: وليس حمله روايته وسرد ألفاظه بل العلم بمعانيه ومخارجه وطرقه ومناهجه

DAMGHANI:v1p191/r14.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r14.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r14.claim: The believing man from Pharaoh's family is Ḥizbīl, according to Dāmghānī.
DAMGHANI:v1p191/r14.anchor: " وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون " وهو حزبيل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r6.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r6.claim: The man whom Pharaoh’s people consider killing for saying “My Lord is God” is identified as Moses.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r8.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p328#2/r8.claim: The believer from Pharaoh’s family, including the man who warns Moses in the city, is identified as Ḥizqīl; another name given is Sharwān.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r1.claim: Bahtān means lying; some call it the highest degree of lying, when the target knows the lie is false.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r1.anchor: البهتان : الكذب . وقيل : إنه أعلى درجات الكذب وهو أن يكذب الرجل لمن يعلم منه انه يعلم كذبه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r2.claim: Yā lil-bahīta is a cry about lying; bahata can also mean a person was stunned.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r2.anchor: والعرب تقول يا للبهيتة ، أي : يا للكذب . ويقال بهت الرجل : إذا دهش .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r3.claim: The source records four vocalized forms of the word baht.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r3.anchor: وفيه أربع لغات بهت وبهت وبهت وبهت .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r4.claim: A Qurʾanic sense of bahtān is lying, as in the declaration that an accusation is a great falsehood.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r4.anchor: أحدها : الكذب . ومنه قوله تعالى في النور : ﴿ سبحانك هذا بهتان عظيم ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r5.claim: A second sense is fornication, in the pledge not to bring a fabricated sexual accusation.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r5.anchor: والثاني : الزنى . ومنه قوله تعالى في الممتحنة : ﴿ ولا يأتين ببهتان يفترينه ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r6.claim: A third sense is unlawful property, as in taking it as a false charge and manifest sin.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p193/r6.anchor: والثالث : الحرام . ومنه قوله تعالى في سورة النساء : ﴿ أتأخذونه بهتانا وإثما مبينا ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r1.speaker: شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r1.claim: ʿAlī ibn ʿUbayd Allāh defines āl as anyone referring to a relied-upon person or thing, by kinship or cause; its root carries return or becoming.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r1.anchor: قال شيخنا علي بن عبيد الله : الآل : اسم لكل من رجع إلى معتمد عليه فيما رجع فيه إليه .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r2.claim: Taʾwīl is named because meaning is referred back from the wording’s apparent sense; an equivalent explanation is bayān or tafsīr.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r2.anchor: لما يؤول فيه ظاهر اللفظ في حقيقته : انه تأويل ، لأن الأمر رجع فيه إلى غير ما هو ظاهره .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r3.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r3.claim: Āl can mean a man’s household and relatives by descent; the believer is Pharaoh’s kin, not an Israelite, explaining Pharaoh’s acceptance of his plea about Moses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r3.anchor: أحدها : أهل بيت الرجل المتكنفين بنسبه . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحجر : ﴿ فلما جاء آل لوط المرسلون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r4.speaker: أبو بكر من أصحابنا
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r4.claim: Abū Bakr of the author’s associates says the believer is Pharaoh’s kin, not an Israelite, explaining Pharaoh’s acceptance of his plea about Moses.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r4.anchor: ولهذا قبل منه فرعون في ترك قتل موسى ولم يكن من بني إسرائيل ، ذكره أبو بكر من أصحابنا في التفسير .

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r5.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r5.claim: Āl can mean a man’s descendants, however far down the lineage extends.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r5.anchor: والثاني : ذرية الرجل وإن سفل نسبهم منه . ومنه قوله تعالى في آل عمران :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r6.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r6.claim: Āl can mean the adherents of a person’s religion, as in references to Pharaoh’s people being drowned or punished.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r6.anchor: والثالث : أهل دين الرجل ، ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ^ ( وأغرقنا آل فرعون ) ^

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r7.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r7.claim: In the phrase about what was left by Moses and Aaron’s āl, āl is an extra connective; the sense is what Moses and Aaron left.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p121#2/r7.anchor: والرابع : صلة في الكلام . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة : ^ ( وبقية مما ترك آل موسى وآل هارون ) ^ ، أي : مما ترك موسى وهارون .

NAHHAS:v4p31/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p31/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p31/r1.claim: أن يقول is accusative with the sense لأن يقول.
NAHHAS:v4p31/r1.anchor: في موضع نصب أي لأن يقول

NAHHAS:v4p31/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p31/r2.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p31/r2.claim: Sibawayh says the nūn is deleted from يكن because the form is frequent; Abu al-Abbas says it is an inflectional nūn.
NAHHAS:v4p31/r2.anchor: حذفت النون لكثرة الاستعمال على قول سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r1.claim: من آل فرعون may attach to يكتم, meaning he conceals his faith from Pharaoh's people; on this parse the verse does not show that the believer was related to Pharaoh.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r1.anchor: يحتمل أن يكون متعلقا ب " يكتم " بعده أي: يكتمه من آل فرعون.

SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r2.claim: The apparent parse makes من آل فرعون an omitted adjectival phrase describing رجل; the ordering noun, nearby prepositional phrase, then clause is especially apt and implies he was from Pharaoh's family.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r2.anchor: والثاني: - وهو الظاهر - أنه متعلق بمحذوف صفة لرجل. وجاء هنا على أحسن ترتيب:

SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r3.claim: Some reject attachment to يكتم because Arabic does not say كتمت من فلان; كتمت takes two direct objects, as in 4:42 and the cited, unattributed poem.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28/r3.anchor: وقد رد بعضهم الأول: بأنه لا يقال: كتمت من فلان كذا، إنما يقال: كتمت فلانا كذا،

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r1.claim: أن يقول means either because he says or on account of saying.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r1.anchor: أي: كراهة أن يقول أو لأن يقول.

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r2.claim: The common reading has the ʿayn in رجل vocalized with ḍamma, the standard form; al-Aʿmash and ʿAbd al-Warith quiesce it, a Tamim and Najd dialect.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r2.anchor: والعامة على ضم عين " رجل " وهي الفصحى. والأعمش وعبد الوارث على تسكينها، وهي لغة تميم ونجد.

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari permits supplying a deleted noun of time, وقت أن يقول, and takes the question to rebuke killing him immediately after hearing the claim without reflection.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " ولك أن تقدر مضافا محذوفا أي: وقت أن يقول. والمعنى: أتقتلونه ساعة سمعتم

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r4.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r4.claim: The Sheikh rejects the omitted-time parse: a time noun may be supplied with an explicit verbal noun, as in صياح الديك, but not with أن يصيح; grammarians state this rule.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r4.anchor: وهذا الذي أجازه رده الشيخ: بأن تقدير هذا الوقت لا يجوز إلا مع المصدر المصرح به

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r5.claim: وقد جاءكم is a circumstantial clause of either the object or the subject; the indefinite object permits a circumstantial adjunct because it occurs in a question, where indefiniteness may be used initially.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#2/r5.anchor: قوله: " وقد جاءكم " جملة حالية يجوز أن تكون من المفعول.

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r1.claim: Some is partitive: the believer understates Moses's due in order to seem impartial rather than zealously partisan.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r1.anchor: " بعض " على بابها، وإنما قال ذلك ليهضم موسى عليه السلام بعض حقه

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r2.claim: Some others take بعض to mean all, citing lines by Labid, ʿAmr ibn Shuyaym, and an unnamed poet; the author says the last two do not prove this, while Labid's line offers some evidence because death comes to everyone.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r2.anchor: وهذا أحسن من قول غيره: إنها بمعنى كل، وأنشدوا قول لبيد:

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r3.speaker: المازني
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r3.claim: Al-Mazani recounts Abu ʿUbayda's objection about feminine tāʾ after the alif in علقى; al-Mazani explains that this is an extension alif, which can take tāʾ to mark a unit, unlike a feminine alif.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r3.anchor: قلت: ومسألة المازني معه أن أبا عبيدة قال للمازني: " ما أكذب النحويين!!

SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r4.speaker: المازني
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r4.claim: Al-Mazani explains that علقى was not nunated because it named a particular thing; its extended alif behaves like feminine tāʾ in making a proper name indeclinable, as with فاطمة.
SAMIN-DURR:40:28#3/r4.anchor: وأما عدم تنوين " علقى " فلأنه سمى بها شيئا بعينه

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r4.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r4.claim: One report in tafsir names the believing man of Pharaoh's household Samʿān.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r4.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن هذا الرجل أعني مؤمن آل فرعون، كان أن يسمى سمعان

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r5.speaker: التفسير
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r5.claim: Another reported view gives the man's name as Habib.

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r6.claim: One parsing makes “from Pharaoh's household” an adjective of man and supplies minhum with “concealing his faith,” meaning he hid it from them.

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r7.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r7.claim: Alternatively, “concealing his faith” modifies “man”: he was a believer from Pharaoh's household who concealed his faith.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r7.anchor: ويكون يكتم من صفة رجل، فيكون المعنى: وقال رجل مؤمن يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r8.claim: The clause means “because he says, My Lord is God.”

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r9.claim: The clear signs are signs of prophethood that demonstrate the man's truthfulness.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r9.anchor: أي بما يدل على صدقه من آيات النبوة

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r10.claim: If the man is lying, the lie harms him and does not harm his opponents.

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r11.claim: Although a Prophet's full promise comes to pass, saying “some” imposes the argument with its easiest consequence; it does not deny that all of it will occur.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r11.anchor: وهذا من لطيف المسائل، لأن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - إذا وعد وعدا

ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r12.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r12.speaker: الشاعر
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r12.claim: An unnamed poet uses “some of his need” to illustrate the use of “some” as the easiest part of an argument.
ZAJJAJ:v4p371/r12.anchor:
ومثل هذا قول الشاعر:
قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته

ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n19/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n19/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n19/r1.claim: Asad compares this believing man with the believer in the parable at 36:20-27, especially note 15.
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n19/r1.anchor: Cf. the parable of the believer in 36:20-27 and, in particular, the corresponding note 15.

ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r1.claim: Asad glosses the accusation literally as "a liar".
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r1.anchor: Lit., "a liar". As regards my rendering of musrif as

ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r2.claim: Asad renders musrif as one who wastes his own self, drawing on his note 21 on 10:12.
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r2.anchor: As regards my rendering of musrif as "one who wastes [or "has wasted"] his own self", see note 21 on the last sentence of 10:12.

ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r3.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r3.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r3.claim: Asad reads the believer's argument as saying Moses' convincing message itself proves he is not spiritually self-destructive through a false claim to divine inspiration.
ASAD-NOTES:40:27#n20/r3.anchor: Thus, the anonymous believer spoken of here argues that the message brought by Moses is so convincing that, by itself, it is a proof

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r1.speaker: أبو عمرو
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r1.claim: Abu Amr reads رجل with a still ج; the other readers use the ordinary vowel on ج.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r1.anchor: عن أبي عمرو: وقال رجل مؤمن [غافر/ 28] ساكنة الجيم. وقرأ الباقون: رجل .

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r2.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r2.claim: Both رجل and رَجُل are regular Arabic variants, comparable to سَبُع/سَبْع and عَضُد/عَضْد.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p108#2/r2.anchor: رجل ورجل وسبع وسبع، وعضد التحقيق على هذا النحو مستمر كثير.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r10.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r10.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r10.claim: A transmission from Abu Amr makes the jīm of رجل silent; Abu Amr thought it was clipped vowel pronunciation used for ease.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r10.anchor: قال حدثنا محمد بن يحيى القطعى عن عبيد عن أبى عمرو ﴿ رجل ﴾ ساكنة الجيم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r11.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r11.speaker: الباقون وأبو عمرو في غير هذه الرواية
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r11.claim: The remaining readers, and Abu Amr in other transmissions, pronounce رجل with ḍamma on the jīm.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p569/r11.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وأبو عمرو فى غير هذه الرواية ﴿ رجل ﴾ بضم الجيم

NASHR:v1p294/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p294/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p294/r1.claim: For the discussed lām assimilation, a preceding consonant permits assimilation; with a preceding sukūn and open following vowel it is normally clear, except the frequent lām of قال, which assimilates.

NASHR:v1p279/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p279/r3.speaker: ابن مجاهد، وابن شنبوذ، وأبو بكر الداجوني
NASHR:v1p279/r3.claim: Most count jazm absolutely as a blocker; Ibn Mujahid’s school does so, while Ibn Shanabudh and al-Dajuni do not. The common view counts it for near pairs and permits both elsewhere except an open letter after sukūn, making disagreement weak for يؤت سعة but strong elsewhere.
NASHR:v1p279/r3.anchor: وهو مذهب أبي بكر بن مجاهد وأصحابه وبعضهم لم يعتد به مطلقا، وهو مذهب ابن شنبوذ

NASHR:v1p173/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Yahya died in 288 AH; al-Dani calls him the foremost of Abu al-Harith's students.
NASHR:v1p173/r1.anchor: (وتوفي محمد بن يحيى) سنة ثمان وثمانين ومائتين، وكان شيخا كبيرا

NASHR:v1p173/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r2.claim: Al-Batti died shortly after 300 AH and was a leading, honest qāriʾ; al-Dani counts him among Muhammad ibn Yahya's most prominent students.
NASHR:v1p173/r2.anchor: (وتوفي البطي) بعيد الثلاثمائة، وكان مقرئا صادقا متصدرا جليلا

NASHR:v1p173/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r3.claim: Al-Qantari died around 310 AH and was a precise, well-known, sought-after, accepted qāriʾ.
NASHR:v1p173/r3.anchor: (وتوفي القنطري) في حدود سنة عشر وثلاثمائة، وكان مقرئا ضابطا معروفا

NASHR:v1p173/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r4.claim: Thaʿlab died in Jumada I 291 AH; he was a major trusted scholar of readings and the Kufians' imam in grammar and language.
NASHR:v1p173/r4.anchor: (وتوفي ثعلب) في جمادى الأولى سنة إحدى وتسعين ومائتين، وكان ثقة كبير المحل

NASHR:v1p173/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj died shortly before 300 AH and was a prominent, precise qāriʾ and grammarian.
NASHR:v1p173/r5.anchor: (وتوفي محمد بن الفرج) قبيل سنة ثلاثمائة، وكان مقرئا نحويا عارفا ضابطا

NASHR:v1p173/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r6.claim: According to al-Dhahabi, Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad died after 307 AH; he was Nisibin's skilled, precise reading authority and a leading student of al-Duri.
NASHR:v1p173/r6.anchor: (وتوفي جعفر بن محمد) بعد سنة سبع وثلاثمائة فيما قاله الذهبي

NASHR:v1p173/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r7.claim: Ibn al-Jalanda died in the 340s AH and was an established, expert qāriʾ; al-Dani praises his precision.
NASHR:v1p173/r7.anchor: (وتوفي ابن الجلندا) سنة بضع وأربعين وثلاثمائة، وكان مقرئا متصدرا متقنا ضابطا

NASHR:v1p173/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r8.claim: Ibn Dizwayh died after 330 AH and was a trusted, well-known narrator famed for precision.
NASHR:v1p173/r8.anchor: (وتوفي ابن ديزويه) بعد الثلاثين وثلاثمائة، وكان ثقة معروفا راويا شهيرا

NASHR:v1p173/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p173/r9.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p173/r9.claim: Al-Dhahabi dates Abu Uthman's death after 310 AH; al-Dani calls him one of al-Duri's senior students.
NASHR:v1p173/r9.anchor: (وتوفي أبو عثمان) بعد سنة عشر وثلاثمائة في قول الذهبي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r1.claim: Reported identifications make the believer a Copt and Pharaoh’s cousin or heir and police chief, an Israelite, or an outsider to both groups.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r1.anchor: قيل كان قبطيا ابن عم فرعون وكان يجري مجرى ولي العهد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r2.claim: For the Israelite or outsider identifications, he is called one of Pharaoh’s people because he entered their circle and concealed his faith by outwardly professing their religion from fear.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r2.anchor: ووصفه على هذين القولين بكونه من آل فرعون باعتبار دخوله في زمرتهم وإظهار أنه على دينهم وملتهم تقية وخوفا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r3.claim: Another parse attaches min āli Firʿawn to concealing his faith, restricting the concealed believer to Pharaoh’s household rather than Moses’ followers; stopping after believer is then possible.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r4.claim: The objection says katama takes a direct object, not min; al-Ālūsī answers that lexicographers allow min with its first object, though the adjective attachment is more apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r4.anchor: واعترض بأن كتم يتعدى بنفسه دون من فيقال : كتمت فلانا كذا دون كتمت من فلان

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r5.claim: The more apparent parse makes the phrase a second adjective of the man and takes his descent from Pharaoh’s family literally.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r5.anchor: نعم تعلقه بذلك خلاف الظاهر بل الظاهر تعلقه بمحذوف وقع صفة ثانية لرجل والظاهر على هذا كونه من آل فرعون حقيقة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r6.claim: The believer is variously named Shamaʿan, Kharbil, Hizbil, or Habib.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r6.anchor: واسمه قيل : شمعان بشين معجمة وقيل : خربيل بخاء معجمة مكسورة وراء مهملة ساكنة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r7.speaker: عيسى وعبد الوارث وعبيد بن عقيل وحمزة بن القاسم عن أبي عمرو
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r7.claim: These authorities read rajul with a still jīm, a dialect of Tamim and Najd.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r7.anchor: وقرأ عيسى وعبد الوارث وعبيد بن عقيل وحمزة بن القاسم عن أبي عمرو ( رجل ) بسكون الجيم وهي لغة تميم ونجد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r8.claim: The question means are you intending to kill him: it names the result, killing, while intending is the cause; its interrogative force does not require an actual killing.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r8.anchor: أي أتقصدون قتله فهو مجاز ذكر فيه المسبب وأريد السبب

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r9.claim: The phrase means because he says my Lord is God.

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows an omitted time noun, meaning would you kill him at the moment you hear him speak, without examining his case.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r10.anchor: وجوز الزمخشري كون ( أن يقول ) على تقدير مضاف أي وقت أن يقول فحذف الظرف

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r11.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r11.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that a complement standing for a temporal noun must be an explicit verbal noun or a durative mā clause, not the non-explicit أن construction.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r11.anchor: ورده أبو حيان بأن القائم مقام الظرف لا يكون إلا المصدر الصريح كجئت صياح الديك أو ما كان بما الدوامية

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r12.speaker: ابن جني
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r12.claim: Ibn Jinni, like al-Zamakhshari, expressly permits the proposed construction; al-Ālūsī says this settles the objection.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r12.anchor: وفيه أن ابن جني كالزمخشري صرح بالجواز وكل إمام

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r13.claim: The clear proofs comprise the miracles and numerous arguments that attest Moses’ truthfulness; the circumstantial clause may describe the killer or the man killed.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r13.anchor: الشاهدة على صدقه من المعجزات والاستدلالات الكثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r14.claim: The sound feminine plural can convey abundance when definite, as the context supports here.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r14.anchor: وجمع المؤنث السالم وإن شاع أنه للقلة لكنه إذا دخلت عليه أل يفيد الكثرة بمعونة المقام

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r15.claim: Calling God the Lord of all of them gently draws them toward admitting that Moses’ Lord is their Lord too.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r15.anchor: أي من عند من نسب إليه الربوبية وهو ربكم لا ربه وحده وهذا استدراج إلى الأعتراف

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r16.claim: The believer reasons that saying my Lord is God, or their saying our lord is Pharaoh, warrants no killing; since Moses names their true Lord too, he deserves respect, not betrayal.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r16.anchor: وفي ( أن يقول ربي الله إلى من ربكم ) نكتة جليلة وهي أن من يقول ربي الله أو فلان لا يقتضي

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r17.claim: The cautious believer says that if Moses lies, the burden of his lie falls on him and there is no need to kill him to avert it.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r17.anchor: لا يتخطاه وبال كذبه فيحتاج في دفعه إلى قتله

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r18.claim: Even a partial fulfillment of Moses’ warning would be dangerous; warning against a part implies that the whole would be worse, while also sounding fair-minded.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r18.anchor: فلا أقل من أن يصيبكم بعض الذي يعدكم أو يعدكموه وفيه مبالغة في التحذير فإنه إذا حذرهم من إصابة البعض أفاد أنه مهلك مخوف

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r19.claim: One view takes the part as a worldly punishment, one of Moses’ promised punishments and the one more plausibly expected by Pharaoh’s people.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r19.anchor: وقيل : المراد يصبكم ما يعدكم من عذاب الدنيا وهو بعض مواعيده كأنه خوفهم بما هو أظهر احتمالا عندهم

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r20.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r20.claim: Abu ʿUbayda allows baʿḍ to mean all and cites Labid’s verse; al-Ālūsī notes that the verse is better read literally as referring to the death of one’s own self.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r20.anchor: وعن أبي عبيدة أنه فسر البعض بالكل أيضا وأنشد قول لبيد

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r21.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r21.claim: Al-Zamakhshari sharply criticizes Abu ʿUbayda’s interpretation if the report attributing it to him is sound.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r21.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : إن صحت الرواية عن أبي عبيدة في ذلك فقد حق فيه قول المازني

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r22.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r22.claim: Al-Zajjaj keeps baʿḍ in its ordinary sense: the believer establishes an unanswerable proof and shows the merit of deliberation over haste.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r22.anchor: وذهب الزجاج إلى أن ( بعض ) فيه على ظاهره والمراد إلزام الحجة وإبانة فضل المتأني على المستعجل

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r23.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r23.claim: The maxim that baʿḍ can mean all is not established by the cited poetry; in Labid’s line, some souls means the speaker himself, so the ordinary partitive meaning remains.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r23.anchor: على أن البعض فيه على ظاهره والمراد به نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r24.speaker: عمرو القطامي
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r24.claim: The patient person’s attaining some need is cited in discussion of whether baʿḍ means all; al-Ālūsī treats the line as supporting the literal-part reading.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r24.anchor: وأنشدوا لذلك قول عمرو القطامي : قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته وقد يكون مع المستعجل الزلل

ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r25.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r25.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r25.claim: A second poetic citation is offered for using baʿḍ to mean all, but al-Ālūsī says the wording does not require that sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p63#2/r25.anchor: وأنشدوا المجيء بمعنى كل قول الشاعر : إن الأمور إذا الأحداث دبرها دون الشيوخ فرى في بعضها خللا

ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r1.claim: The believer’s final argument has two readings: if Moses were an extravagant liar, God would not guide him to proofs and support him with miracles; or God would abandon and destroy him, leaving no need to kill him.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r1.anchor: احتجاج آخر ذو وجهين أحدهما أنه لو كان مسرفا كذابا لما هداه الله تعالى إلى البينات

ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r2.claim: The man probably intends the first argument but hints at the second to soften his hearers; he indirectly calls Pharaoh extravagant in killing and corruption and a liar in claiming divinity.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r2.anchor: ولعله أراد الأول وأوهمهم أنه أراد الثاني لتلين شكيمتهم وعرض لفرعون بأنه مسرف أي في القتل والفساد كذاب في ادعاء الربوبية

ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r3.claim: The final sentence may be attached to either conditional or to both.
ALUSI-FULL:v24p65/r3.anchor: فالجملة مستأنفة متعلقة بالشرطية الأولى أو بالثانية أو بهما

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r1.claim: Arabic eloquence was the Arabs' foremost distinction, and they displayed their challenge by hanging the seven celebrated odes at the Kaaba; the Prophet's unmatched Quran therefore proved divine origin.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r1.anchor: والبلاغة قد بلغت في ذلك العهد حدها وكان فيها فخارهم حتى علقت السبع بباب الكعبة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r2.claim: Repeated, accurate Quranic reports about unseen events are extraordinary by ordinary standards; that unusual success is itself the relevant sense of a miracle.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r2.anchor: فإن الإخبار عن الغائبات مع التكرر والإصابة غير معتاد ولا معنى لكونه معجزا غير هذا

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r3.claim: Although one or two correct predictions need not be supernatural, repeated successes can be; the Quran contains enough unseen reports to exceed customary chance.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r3.anchor: لا يلزم من عدم كون الإصابة في المرة والمرتين من الخوارق أن لا تكون الإصابة في الكرات الكثيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r4.claim: Astrologers' false predictions have no evidentiary force, while accurate eclipse predictions come from their ordinary calculations; Quranic reports of the unseen are unlike these.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r4.anchor: ما كان كاذبا منها لا إحتجاج وما كان صادقا وتكررت الإصابة فيه كالكسوف والخسوف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r5.claim: The objection from soothsayers is answered as the parallel objection from sorcery is answered.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r5.anchor: وأما أخبار الكهنة فالقول فيها كما في السحر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r6.claim: If the Torah's unseen reports were abundant, extraordinary, and challenged, they too would be miracles and signs of the truth of the one who brought them; this concession does no harm.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r6.anchor: فلأن ما في التوراة من الأخبار بالغيب إن كان كثيرا خارقا للعادة ووقع التحدي به

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r7.claim: The objection does not affect a combined account of the Quran's miracle; if unseen reports alone are proposed, the Quran is miraculous as a whole even if passages without such reports are not individually miraculous.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r7.anchor: فلأنه لا يرد على من يقول وجه الإعجاز مجموع ما تقدم أصلا ومن يقول وجهه مجرد الأخبار بالغيب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r8.claim: The denial that the Prophet was taught poetry (36:69) answers the supposed poetic contradiction; the alleged differences in 4:82 concern either defective eloquence or conflicting accounts of the past, neither of which occurs in the Quran.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r8.anchor: لأن المراد به أحد أمرين الأول الإختلاف المناقض للبلاغة والثاني الإختلاف فيما أخبر عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r9.claim: Some alleged contradictions are not Quran because they lack mass transmission; other differences of wording reflect different circumstances while describing one underlying reality, such as Adam's origin from earth.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r9.anchor: على أن أمثال بعض ما ذكر من الإختلاف ليس بقرآن لأنه لم يتواتر وأمثال البعض الآخر إختلاف مقال لإختلاف الأحوال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reconciles verses that deny and affirm questioning by placing the denial before the second trumpet and the affirmation afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r10.anchor: ابن عباس حين سأله رجل عن آيات من هذا القبيل بأن نفي المسألة قبل النفخة الثانية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r11.speaker: السدي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says questioning is denied while people are occupied with swooning, judgment, and crossing the bridge, but affirmed at other times.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r11.anchor: والسدي بأن نفي المسألة عند تشاغلهم بالصعق والمحاسبة والجواز على الصراط

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r12.claim: Ibn Masud distinguishes the negated asking as people seeking pardon from one another, while the affirmed questioning retains its apparent sense.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r12.anchor: وابن مسعود بأن المسألة المنفية طلب بعضهم العفو من بعض والمثبتة على ظاهر معناها

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r13.claim: The first of the two 'what prevented people from believing' passages refers to God's will that earlier peoples' punishment befall them or that they see punishment in the hereafter; divine will is the true cause, so this is no contradiction.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r13.anchor: إرادة الله تعالى مانعة من وقوع ما ينافي المراد فهذا حصر في السبب الحقيقي

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r14.claim: The second passage refers to people's ordinary astonishment at a human messenger, not a true impediment; that customary obstacle can coexist with faith and does not contradict the first passage.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r14.anchor: إلا إستغراب بعثة البشر رسولا وهو مدلول القول إلتزاما والدال لا يناسب المانعية

ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r15.claim: Repeated wording or meaning always serves a purpose, including breadth of expression, display of eloquence, and added emphasis or intensification.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p29/r15.anchor: وأما التكرار اللفظي والمعنوي فلا يخلو عن فائدة لا تحصل من غير تكرار كبيان إتساع العبارة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r1.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r1.claim: Twenty-one Companions transmitted that the Quran was revealed in seven ahruf, and Abu Ubayda explicitly judged the report mass-transmitted.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r1.anchor: روى أحد وعشرون صحابيا حديث نزول القرآن على سبعة أحرف حتى نص أبو عبيدة على تواتره

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r2.speaker: عثمان
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r2.claim: On the pulpit Uthman asked witnesses to testify that the Prophet said the Quran was revealed in seven ahruf, all sound and sufficient; many stood and Uthman joined their testimony.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r2.anchor: أن عثمان رضي الله عنه قال على المنبر أذكر الله رجلا سمع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r3.claim: One view treats the seven ahruf report as an obscure expression whose meaning cannot be known; al-Alusi replies that the word's ambiguity alone does not make the report obscure.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r3.anchor: أنه من المشكل الذي لا يدري لإشتراك الحرف وفيه أن مجرد الإشتراك لا يستدعي ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r4.speaker: عياض
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r4.claim: Qadi Iyad takes seven as a conventional number for abundance, as Arabs also use seventy and seven hundred for large quantities.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r4.anchor: أن المراد التكثير لا حقيقة العدد وقد جروا على تكثير الآحاد بالسبعة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r5.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r5.claim: A report from Ubayy says Gabriel first asked the Prophet to recite on one harf, while Michael urged him to request more until the count reached seven.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r5.anchor: حديث أبي كما رواه النسائي أن جبريل وميكائيل أتياني فقعد جبريل عن يميني

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r6.speaker: أبي بكرة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r6.claim: In Abu Bakra's report, the Prophet knew the requested allowance had reached its limit when he looked to Michael and Michael fell silent.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r6.anchor: حديث أبي بكرة الذي في آخره فنظرت إلى ميكائيل فسكت فعلمت أنه قد إنتهت العدة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r7.claim: These reports indicate an exact limit of seven, not a loose expression for abundance; the wording in a paucity plural also suggests a limited number.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r7.anchor: أقوى دليل على إرادة الإنحصار بل في جمع القلة نوع إشارة إلى عدم الكثرة

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r8.claim: A third view identifies the seven ahruf with the seven canonical readings, but words with seven variants are rare and some words are read in more than seven ways.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r8.anchor: إن المراد بها سبع قرآت وفيه أن ذلك لا يوجد في كلمة واحدة إلا نادر

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r9.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r9.claim: Al-Suyuti calls it gross ignorance to suppose that the seven ahruf mean the seven readings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r9.anchor: قال السيوطي قد ظن كثير من القوم أن المراد بها القرآت السبعة وهو جهل قبيح

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r10.speaker: إبن عيينة
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r10.claim: Ibn Uyayna and others hold that the seven ahruf are seven synonymous expressions for a shared meaning, such as aqbil, taʿal, hallum, ʿajjil, and asriʿ.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r10.anchor: وإليه ذهب إبن عيينة وجمع وأيد برواية حتى بلغ سبعة أحرف

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r11.claim: A supporting report says all seven forms are healing and sufficient, but forbids ending a verse of punishment with mercy or mercy with punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r11.anchor: ما لم تختم آية عذاب برحمة أو رحمة بعذاب

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r12.speaker: إبن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r12.claim: When a man could not pronounce 'al-athim,' Ibn Masud told him to say 'al-fajir' instead.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r12.anchor: أن إبن مسعود أقرأ رجلا ( إن شجرة الزقوم طعام الأثيم ) فقال الرجل

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r13.claim: Al-Alusi treats synonym substitution as a temporary concession for illiterate people struggling with a fixed wording; it was later abrogated, since otherwise recitation by meaning would erase exact-word worship and many subtleties and rulings.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r13.anchor: أن ذلك كان رخصة لعسر تلاوته بلفظ واحد على الأميين ثم نسخ وإلا لجازت روايته بالمعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r14.claim: A fifth view says the ahruf are pronunciation modes such as assimilation, clarity, emphatic or light articulation, lengthening, shortening, and stress.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r14.anchor: أن المراد بها كيفية النطق بالتلاوة من إدغام وإظهار وتفخيم وترقيق وإشباع ومد

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r15.claim: Pronunciation modes do not vary the word or meaning; the word remains one, so this view offers no substantial benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r15.anchor: أن ذلك ليس من الإختلاف الذي يتنوع فيه اللفظ والمعنى واللفظ الواحد بهذه الصفات

ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r16.claim: A sixth view, held by many, identifies the seven ahruf as seven categories; the segment begins listing those categories but does not name them here.
ALUSI-FULL:v1p20/r16.anchor: أن المراد سبعة أصناف وعليه كثيرون ثم أختلفوا في تعيينها فقيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r2.speaker: مقاتل والسدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r2.claim: Muqātil and al-Suddī say the believer was an Egyptian, Pharaoh's cousin, and the man described in Q 28:20.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل والسدي: كان قبطيا ابن عم فرعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r3.speaker: قوم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r3.claim: Some say the believing man was an Israelite, with min āli Firʿawn understood as describing whom he concealed his faith from.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r3.anchor: وقال قوم: كان إسرائيليا، ومجاز الآية: وقال رجل مؤمن يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر العلماء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and most scholars give the man's name as Ḥuzayl.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r4.anchor: وكان اسمه حزئيل عند ابن عباس، وأكثر العلماء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq gives the man's name as Jibrān.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r6.claim: Another reported name for the believer is Ḥabīb.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r6.anchor: وقيل: كان اسم الرجل الذي آمن من آل فرعون حبيبا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r7.claim: The phrase an yaqūla means because he says, 'My Lord is God.'
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r7.anchor: {أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله} لأن يقول ربي الله

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r8.claim: The clear proofs are what indicate Moses' truthfulness.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r9.claim: If Moses is lying, the liability for his lie is his own and it will not harm you.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r10.claim: If Moses is truthful and they reject him, some of what he threatens will reach them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r11.speaker: أبو عبيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayd says baʿḍ, 'some,' means the whole: if they kill Moses while he is truthful, all the threatened punishment will strike them.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r11.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: المراد بالبعض الكل، أي: إن قتلتموه وهو صادق أصابكم ما يتوعدكم به من العذاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r12.speaker: الليث
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r12.claim: Al-Layth treats baʿḍ as an additional particle, so the sense is that what Moses promises will strike them.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r13.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r13.speaker: أهل المعاني
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r13.claim: The rhetoricians retain the ordinary sense 'some': even a portion of the threatened punishment would mean their destruction, so mention of a part establishes the whole.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r13.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: هذا على الظاهر في الحجاج كأنه قال: أقل ما في صدقه أن يصيبكم بعض الذي يعدكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r14.claim: Mus'rif here means an associator of partners with God, and kadhdhāb means a liar against God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r15.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r15.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r15.claim: Ibn ʿAmr told ʿUrwa that the worst assault on the Prophet was when ʿUqba ibn Abī Muʿayṭ choked him at the Kaʿba; Abū Bakr intervened and quoted the believer's words. No grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p146/r15.anchor: قلت لعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: أخبرني بأشد ما صنعه

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.claim: Poetry permits forms excluded from ordinary speech, including declining diptotes and deleting material that speech normally retains.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.anchor: اعلم أنه يجوز في الشعر ما لا يجوز في الكلام من صرف ما لا ينصرف

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.claim: Poets sometimes lengthen patterns like مساجد and منابر to مساجيد and منابير; al-Farazdaq's الدنانير illustrates the extension.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.anchor: مساجد ومنابر فيقولون مساجيد ومنابير شبهوه بما جمع على غير واحده

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.claim: Poetry can restore the underlying form of weak endings: examples include رادد for راد and ضننوا for ضنوا, witnessed by Qaʿnab's line.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.anchor: وقد يبلغون بالمعتل الأصل فيقولون رادد في راد وضننوا في

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.claim: Some speakers geminate words in pause and retain that weight in poetic connected speech, as in سبسبا and كلكلا; several poets illustrate the pattern.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.anchor: فهم يجرونه في الوصل على حاله في الوقف نحو سبسبا وكلكلا

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.claim: Poets also tolerate dispreferred word order when the expression remains complete; the intended prose order is وقل ما يدوم وصال.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.anchor: حتى يضعوه في غير موضعه لأنه مستقيم ليس فيه نقص

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.claim: In poetry, سواء and the particle كاف may be used like ordinary nouns because سواء means غير and كاف means مثل.

SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.claim: Sībawayh says poets seek a grammatical rationale for every necessity, and that the examples exceed what this brief survey can list.
SIBAWAYH:اعلمأنهيجوزفيالشعرمالايجوزفيالك.anchor: وليس شئ يضطرون إليه إلا وهم يحاولون به وجها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: The active participle with alif-lām, as in الضارب زيدا, functions like the relative هذا الذي ضرب زيدا; the article blocks annexation and acts like tanwīn.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: وذلك قولك هذا الضارب زيدا فصار فى معنى هذا الذى ضرب

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: Some accepted Arabic usage says الضارب الرجل by analogy with الحسن الوجه, although their meaning and grammatical conditions differ; this noun pattern permits genitive or accusative use.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: وقد قال قوم من العرب ترضى عربيتهم هذا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: Al-Marrār al-Asadī's التارك البكري بشرا treats بشر as genitive in poetry, by analogy with a form whose tanwīn is blocked.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: When dual or plural participles retain their nūn, their object is accusative, as in الضاربان زيدا and الضاربون الرجل; the Qur'anic المقيمين الصلاة is a parallel.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: أو جمعت فأثبت النون قلت هذان الضاربان زيدا

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: When nūn is dropped from these forms, the following overt noun is normally genitive; examples include الضاربا زيد and الضاربو عمرو.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: جررت وصار الاسم داخلا فى الجار

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: In poetic examples such as الحافظو عورة العشيرة, nūn deletion is not annexation or substitution for nūn but an elision like اللذين, licensed when the phrase grows long.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: للإضافة ولا ليعاقب الاسم النون ولكن حذفوها كما حذفوها من اللذين والذين

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: With a connected object pronoun, as in الضاربوك, the pronoun is genitive, not accusative; a bare ضاربو زيدا is unavailable without the relative article.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: هم الضاربوك وهما الضارباك فالوجه فيه الجر

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: Nūn and tanwīn must be deleted before a connected pronoun because the pronoun is bound to the host, much like these suffixes at a word's end.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: واعلم أن حذف النون والتنوين لازم مع علامة المضمر غير المنفصل لأنه

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.claim: Sībawayh reports two poetic examples retaining nūn before an attached pronoun, while noting that they were said to be fabricated.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكهذاالضاربزيدافصارفىمعنى.anchor: وقد جاء فى الشعر وزعموا أنه مصنوع

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r6.claim: From Pharaoh's family may mean his relatives; alternatively, it attaches to concealing his faith, and the man was an Israelite or a foreign monotheist feigning agreement.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r6.anchor: من أقاربه. وقيل { من } متعلق بقوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r7.claim: The question means, Are you deliberately seeking to kill a man?

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r8.claim: The phrase can mean because he says or at the time he says, without reflection or consideration.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r8.anchor: لأن يقول، أو وقت أن يقول من غير روية وتأمل في أمره

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r9.claim: My Lord is God means God alone, with the same restrictive force as my friend is Zayd.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r9.anchor: وحده وهو في الدلالة على الحصر مثل صديقي زيد

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r10.claim: The numerous proofs are miracles and demonstrations that establish Moses' truthfulness.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r10.anchor: المتكثرة الدالة على صدقه من المعجزات والاستدلالات

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r11.claim: Calling the signs from your Lord presses them to acknowledge the point and gently leads them toward admitting it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r11.anchor: أضافه إليهم بعد ذكر البينات احتجاجا عليهم واستدراجا لهم إلى الاعتراف به

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r12.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r12.claim: If Moses lies, the harm of his lie falls only on him, so there is no need to kill him to avert it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r12.anchor: لا يتخطاه وبال كذبه فيحتاج في دفعه إلى قتله

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r13.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r13.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r13.claim: At least part of the threatened punishment will befall them; warning them with a limited share is rhetorically forceful and displays fairness rather than bias.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r13.anchor: فلا أقل من أن يصيبكم بعضه، وفيه مبالغة في التحذير وإظهار للإنصاف وعدم التعصب

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r14.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r14.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r14.claim: Some means some of the worldly punishment Moses promised, a portion of his threats and the more plausible outcome for the audience.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r14.anchor: أو يصبكم ما يعدكم من عذاب الدنيا وهو بعض مواعيده، كأنه خوفهم بما هو أظهر احتمالا عندهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r15.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r15.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r15.claim: Interpreting some as all by appeal to Labīd's verse is rejected: Labīd meant himself by some of the souls.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r15.anchor: وتفسير ال { بعض } بالكل كقول لبيد:

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r16.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r16.speaker: الرجل المؤمن
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r16.claim: The believer's third argument has two sides: God would not guide and support a liar with signs, and someone God abandons will be destroyed without needing the audience to kill him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:27-28/r16.anchor: احتجاج ثالث ذو وجهين: أحدهما: أنه لو كان مسرفا كذابا

BAYDAWI-FULL:40:28-29/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:28-29/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:28-29/r6.claim: The believer likely intended the first argument while suggesting the second to soften their resistance; he also hints that Pharaoh is the extravagant liar whom God will not guide.
BAYDAWI-FULL:40:28-29/r6.anchor: ولعله أراد به المعنى الأول وخيل إليهم الثاني لتلين شكيمتهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r6.claim: After the two leading figures speak, the account turns to a follower's speech, since people without a divinely bound order tend to divide and some speak despite a ruler's control.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r6.anchor: وكانت عادة من لم يكن لهم نظام من الله رابط أن قلوبهم لا تكاد تجتمع

BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r7.claim: The man is complete in manhood and firmly believes the message Moses brought.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r7.anchor: أي كامل في رجوليته { مؤمن } أي راسخ الإيمان فيما جاء به موسى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r8.claim: He belongs to Pharaoh's elite and leading household, a place from which he can advise while remaining among hostile people.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r8.anchor: من آل فرعون } أي وجوههم ورؤسائهم

BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r9.claim: He conceals his faith intensely from fear, using indirect counsel to stop them from killing Moses; a lone dissenter from a tribe is more vulnerable than someone among a diverse group.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r9.anchor: يخفيه إخفاءا شديدا خوفا على نفسه لأن الواحد إذا شذ عن قبيلة يطمع فيه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r10.claim: He frames their intended killing as an appalling question and calls Moses a man of great physical and moral stature.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r10.anchor: فقال منكرا له غاية الإنكار : { أتقتلون رجلا } أي هو عظيم في الرجال حسا ومعنى

BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r11.claim: He objects that they would kill Moses merely for repeatedly saying his Lord is God, though God has already sent him clear, unambiguous signs.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r11.anchor: لأجل أن { يقول } ولو على سبيل التكرير

BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r12.claim: Since God is Moses' Lord and benefactor, Moses should acknowledge Him; the audience's own dependence on the same Lord should likewise lead them to acknowledge Him.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p506/r12.anchor: وكما أن ربوبيته له اقتضت عنه الاعتراف بها فكذلك ينبغي أن تكون ربوبيته لكم داعية لكم إلى اعترافكم له بها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r1.claim: The believer presents the possibility that Moses is false first because it best dispels suspicion; his lie would harm him alone, not the hearers.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r1.anchor: مقدما القسم الذي هو أنفى للتهمة عنه وأدعى للقبول منه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r2.claim: The nūn is deleted from both instances of yakun to compress the warning under extreme pressure: the believer faces three dangers, including exposure of his faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r2.anchor: حذف النون فقال : { يك كاذبا فعليه }

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r3.claim: He still gives the truthful case its due, balancing fairness with the false case and stating that even some threatened consequence is enough to prove the danger.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r3.anchor: إظهارا للنصفة ودفعا للتهمة عن نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r4.claim: Saying 'some of what he promises' is measured fairness: acceptance brings all promised good, rejection brings all the threatened evil, but even a part is enough as a warning; the verse uses ellipsis between the two cases.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r4.anchor: إشارة إلى أنهم إن وافوه أصابهم جميع ما وعدهموه من الخير , وإلا دهاهم ما توعدهم من الشر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r5.claim: An account in al-Ṣaḥīḥ relates that Abu Bakr cited this verse as Quraysh seized the Prophet's clothing during circumambulation; he embraced him in tears until God delivered him, after attackers tore much of his hair.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r5.anchor: كما في الصحيح عن عبد الله بن عمرو رضي الله عنهما - أبو بكر الصديق رضي الله عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r6.claim: The believer's description of the transgressor and liar chiefly fits Pharaoh, distancing the speaker from him, though it could also be applied to Moses as Pharaoh alleges.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r6.anchor: بما ينطبق إلى فرعون منفرا منه مع صلاحيته لأرادة موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام على ما زعمه فيه فرعون

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r7.claim: An overreacher is one who exceeds bounds by promoting corruption.

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r8.claim: The liar is persistently excessive in lying; plunging into falsehood is the first sign of being abandoned by guidance.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r8.anchor: لأن أول خذلانه تعمقه في الكذب

BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r9.claim: God guides the moderate and truthful; if Moses lies, his lie harms him and he finds no escape, while if he is truthful, their wrongdoing leaves them unable to find rescue from punishment.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p507/r9.anchor: ويهدي من هو مقتصد صادق , فإن كان كاذبا كما زعمتم ضره كذبه

DURR-FULL:v7p285/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r1.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r1.claim: Amr ibn al-As reports that Quraysh seized the Prophet at the Kaaba after he said he forbade ancestral worship; Abu Bakr clung to him, recited the believing man's plea, and cried until they released him.
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص رضي الله عنه قال: ما رأى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم شيئا كان أشد من أن طاف بالبيت ضحى

DURR-FULL:v7p285/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r2.speaker: أنس بن مالك
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r2.claim: Anas says the Prophet was beaten until unconscious, after which Abu Bakr shouted the verse and identified himself to Quraysh as Ibn Abi Quhafa.
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r2.anchor: عن أنس بن مالك رضي الله عنه قال: ضربوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حتى غشي عليه فقام أبو بكر

DURR-FULL:v7p285/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r3.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r3.claim: Asma bint Abi Bakr transmits a similar account of Abu Bakr defending the Prophet by reciting the believing man's words.
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r3.anchor: من حديث أسماء بنت أبي بكر رضي الله عنهما نحوه

DURR-FULL:v7p285/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r4.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r4.claim: Ali calls Abu Bakr the bravest: when Quraysh surrounded the Prophet and no one else approached, Abu Bakr struck and fought them while reciting the verse.
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r4.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال: أيها الناس أخبروني بأشجع الناس قالوا: أنت قال: لا قالوا: فمن قال: أبو بكر رضي الله عنه

DURR-FULL:v7p285/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r5.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r5.claim: Ali contrasts the believing man of Pharaoh, who concealed his faith, with Abu Bakr, who openly declared his faith, and asks whether the former was better.
DURR-FULL:v7p285/r5.anchor: ثم رفع علي رضي عنه بردة كانت عليه فبكى حتى اخضلت لحيته ثم قال: أنشدكم بالله أمؤمن آل فرعون خير أم أبو بكر

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r1.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r1.claim: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ recounts that Quraysh seized the Prophet for forbidding ancestral worship, while Abū Bakr embraced and defended him, reciting this verse through its end.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r1.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص انه سئل : ما اشد ما رايت قريشا بلغوا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ؟

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Pharaoh’s household had only this believer, Pharaoh’s wife, and the believer who warned Moses that the leaders were plotting to kill him.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3266/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله ، عنهما قال : لم يكن في ال فرعون مؤمن غيره وغير امراة فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r1.claim: The waw indicates that the believer spoke outside Pharaoh’s council; a reply in the same exchange would have been narrated without it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r1.anchor: عطف قول هذا الرجل يقتضي أنه قال قوله هذا في غير مجلس شورى فرعون ، لأنه لو كان قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r2.claim: God inspired the man to speak, the first sign of answering Moses’s appeal for refuge; once Pharaoh’s threat spread, the trusted member of his household came to advise him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r2.anchor: والذي يظهر أن الله ألهم هذا الرجل بأن يقول مقالته إلهاما كان أول مظهر من تحقيق الله لاستعاذة موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r3.claim: The question is directed to Pharaoh, who ordered the killing; the next statement identifies him as speaking without a coordinating waw (40:29).
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r3.anchor: وخطابه بقوله : { أتقتلون } موجه إلى فرعون لأن فرعون هو الذي يسند إليه القتل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r4.claim: Some exegetes identify the believer as an Israelite, but Ibn ʿAshur rejects this: the following claim to rule the land fits Pharaoh’s Egyptians, not Israelites.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r4.anchor: ووصفه بأنه من آل فرعون صريح في أنه من القبط ولم يكن من بني إسرائيل خلافا لبعض المفسرين ألا ترى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAshur considers him most likely a relative or close associate of Pharaoh, as آل naturally or figuratively suggests.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r5.anchor: والأظهر أنه كان من قرابة فرعون وخاصته لما يقتضيه لفظ آل من ذلك حقيقة أو مجازا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r6.claim: He was a righteous believer in God and Moses, guided by reflection or by hearing Moses; Ibn ʿAshur compares this to Abu Bakr believing the Prophet on first hearing him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r6.anchor: وما كان إيمانه هذا إلا لأنه كان رجلا صالحا اهتدى إلى توحيد الله إما بالنظر في الأدلة فصدق موسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r7.claim: He continually concealed his faith as protective dissimulation because disclosure would harm him without helping anyone; Ibn ʿAshur compares him with Socrates in Greece.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r7.anchor: وكان كتمه الإيمان متجددا مستمرا تقية من فرعون وقومه إذ علم أن إظهاره الإيمان يضره ولا ينفع غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r8.claim: The man seeks to save Moses by opening debate about him and making Pharaoh question his rejection, rather than provoking immediate hostility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r8.anchor: إلى آخره أن يسعى لحفظ موسى من القتل بفتح باب المجادلة في شأنه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r9.claim: This is not the Israelite in 28:20, who helped Moses shortly before his departure from Egypt; the present story occurs as Moses begins returning. Exodus identifies the earlier man as Israelite.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r9.anchor: وهذا الرجل هو غير الرجل المذكور في سورة القصص في قوله تعالى : { وجاء رجل من أقصى المدينة يسعى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r10.claim: The man was a righteous thinker in monotheistic proofs whose faith settled after hearing Moses; God raises protectors for righteous servants in hardship.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p127/r10.anchor: والظاهر أن الرجل المذكور هنا كان رجلا صالحا نظارا في أدلة التوحيد ولم يستقر الإيمان في قلبه على وجهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r1.claim: The man is said to have been named Habib al-Najjar or Samʿan; Ibn ʿAshur notes that Habib in Ya Sin was one of Jesus’s messengers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r1.anchor: قيل اسم هذا الرجل حبيب النجار وقيل سمعان ، وقد تقدم في سورة ( يس ) أن حبيبا النجار من رسل عيسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r2.claim: The question is one of censure: it is disgraceful to kill someone merely for saying God is his Lord; he neither coerced them to believe nor did more than state his view, so they could accept or reject it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r2.anchor: والاستفهام في { أتقتلون } استفهام إنكار ، أي يقبح بكم أن تقتلوا نفسا لأنه يقول ربي الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r3.claim: An yaqul is governed by an implied lām of purpose, which is often omitted before أن.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r3.anchor: و { أن يقول } . مجرور بلام التعليل المقدرة لأنها تحذف مع ( أن ) كثيرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r4.claim: Moses named God because this was the deity he invoked, unlike the names of the Coptic gods.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r4.anchor: وذكر اسمم الله لأنه الذي ذكره موسى ولم يكن من أسماء آلهة القبط

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r5.claim: After a tactful opening, the believer advances to explicit endorsement of Moses: clear proofs establish his truth, and the God he names is their Lord too.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r5.anchor: فهو ارتقاء في الحجاج بعد أن استأنس في خطاب قومه بالكلام الموجه فارتقى إلى التصريح بتصديق موسى بعلة أنه جاء بالبينات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r6.claim: Al-bayyināt means clear proofs of Moses’s truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r6.anchor: أي الحجج الواضحة بصدقه ، وإلى التصريح بأن الذي سماه الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r7.claim: The clause وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم is circumstantial with respect to رجلا, and the bāʾ in بالبينات indicates accompaniment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p129/r7.anchor: فجملة { وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم } في موضع الحال من قوله : { رجلا } والباء في { بالبينات } للمصاحبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r1.claim: The believer feigns doubt so his speech can entertain both possibilities and avoid being exposed as Moses’s partisan, giving Pharaoh and his council a path to consider the evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r1.anchor: رجوع إلى ضرب من إيهام الشك في صدق موسى ليكون كلامه مشتملا على احتمالي تصديق وتكذيب يتداولهما في كلامه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r2.claim: The conditional clause coordinates with وقد جاءكم بالبينات and is therefore also circumstantial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r2.anchor: فالجملة عطف على جملة { وقد جاءكم بالبينات } فتكون حالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r3.claim: He mentions the possibility of lying first to distance himself from the impression that he is defending Moses and to appear initially concerned for his people.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r3.anchor: وقدم احتمال كذبه على احتمال صدقه زيادة في التباعد عن ظنهم به الانتصار لموسى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r4.claim: He urges them to inspect Moses’s signs rather than kill or follow him hastily: if his claims and warnings fail, the lie harms and brands Moses alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r4.anchor: ومعنى : { وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه } استنزالهم للنظر ، أي فعليكم بالنظر في آياته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r5.claim: If Moses is truthful, some of his threatened calamities will strike and establish his truth; the wording says some because initial portents may persuade them, while persistence in defiance brings all the threats a fortiori.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r5.anchor: وإن تبين لكم صدقه يصبكم بعض ما توعدكم به ، أي تصبكم بوارقه فتعلموا صدقه فتتبعوه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r6.claim: Here promise means a threat, that is, a warning of evil; if they persist in defiance, all that he threatened will strike them a fortiori.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r6.anchor: والمراد بالوعد هنا الوعد بالسوء وهو المسمى بالوعيد . أي فإن استمررتم على العناد يصبكم جميع ما توعدكم به

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r7.claim: When ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayṭ strangled the Prophet at the Kaʿba, Abu Bakr intervened and pushed him away, invoking the believer’s words.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r7.anchor: ويوم جاء عقبة بن أبي معيط إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بفناء الكعبة ) يخنقه بثوبه فأقبل أبو بكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r8.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r8.claim: ʿAli said Abu Bakr’s day was better than the believer from Pharaoh’s household: the believer hid faith, while Abu Bakr openly risked his wealth and life.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r8.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طالب : ( والله ليوم أبي بكر خير من مؤمن آل فرعون ، إن مؤمن آل فرعون رجل يكتم إيمانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAshur judges Abu Bakr’s conviction stronger because he displayed his faith openly while the believer concealed his.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130/r9.anchor: وأقول : كان أبو بكر أقوى يقينا من مؤمن آل فرعون لأن مؤمن آل فرعون كتم إيمانه وأبو بكر أظهر إيمانه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r1.claim: One reading makes this the believer’s explanation of his conditional advice: God will not let a liar persist in a claim against Him but exposes or destroys him, as 69:44–46 says.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r1.anchor: يجوز أنها من قول مؤمن آل فرعون ، فالمقصود منها تعليل قوله : { وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r2.claim: God does not authenticate a liar: a supernatural sign after a challenge establishes the claimant’s truth, since divine confirmation of a liar is impossible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r2.anchor: ولأنه إذا جاءكم بخوارق العادات فقد تبين صدقه لأن الله لا يخرق العادة بعد تحدي المتحدي بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r3.claim: The threatened portion may befall them in this life or the next; the signs themselves could bring disasters such as the flood, locusts, and the remaining signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r3.anchor: أي مما توعدكم بوقوعه في الدنيا ، أو في الآخرة وكيف إذا كانت البينة نفسها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r4.claim: Musرف means one who exceeds what is proper; here the excess is lying against God, the greatest lie, as 6:93 states.
