IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r4.anchor: والمسرف : متجاوز المعروف في شيء ، فالمراد هنا مسرف في الكذب لأن أعظم الكذب أن يكون على الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r5.claim: If excess means excessive lying, كذاب is an explanatory apposition rather than a second predicate, because lying is the only relevant excess here.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r5.anchor: وإذا كان المراد الإسراف في الكذب تعين أن قوله : { كذاب } عطف بيان وليس خبرا ثانيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the sentence is God’s parenthetical commendation of the believer: denying guidance to an excessive liar implies this righteous man speaks from guidance and truth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v24p130#2/r6.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة { إن الله لا يهدي } إلى آخرها جملة معترضة بين كلامي مؤمن آل فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555/r3.claim: The believer’s public challenge shows he confronted Pharaoh more than he merely accommodated him and stated Moses’ prophethood openly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555/r3.anchor: والدليل الثاني: مقالة المؤمن وما صدع به، وأن مكاشفته لفرعون أكثر من مسايرته

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r4.speaker: أبو الفضل الجوهري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r4.claim: In a sermon on the Companions’ merits, Abu al-Fadl al-Jawhari cited God’s preservation of the concealed believer’s speech in scripture and argued that the Prophet’s Companions deserved still greater honor.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r4.anchor: سمعت أبا الفضل الجوهري على المنبر وقد سئل أن يتكلم في شيء من فضائل الصحابة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r5.speaker: عدي بن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r5.claim: Adi ibn Zayd’s couplet says a person should be assessed by his companion, introducing the sermon’s praise of the Companions.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r5.anchor: أنشد [عدي بن زيد] : [الطويل] عن المرء لا تسأل وسل عن قرينه ... فكل قرين بالمقارن مقتد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r6.claim: God memorialized this man in the Qur’an for a statement made in an unbelieving assembly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r6.anchor: وقد أثنى الله على رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون كتم إيمانه وأسره، فجعله الله تعالى في كتابه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r7.claim: Abu al-Fadl contrasts the concealed believer with Umar, who drew his sword in Mecca and swore no longer to worship secretly.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r7.anchor: وأين هو من عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه جرد سيفه بمكة وقال: والله لا عبد الله سرا بعد اليوم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r8.speaker: فرقة والجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r8.claim: One group reads rajul with a still jīm, like ʿaḍud and sabaʿ; the majority pronounce the jīm with ḍamma.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r8.anchor: وقرأت فرقة: «رجل» بسكون الجيم، كعضد وعضد، وسبع وسبع، وقراءة الجمهور بضم الجيم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r9.speaker: السدي وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r9.claim: Al-Suddi and others say the believer belonged to Pharaoh’s family and concealed his faith; on this reading, the clause is an adjective without inversion.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r9.anchor: فقال السدي وغيره: كان من آل فرعون وأهله، وكان يكتم إيمانه، ف يكتم على هذا في موضع الصفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r10.speaker: مقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r10.claim: Muqatil says the believer was Pharaoh’s paternal cousin.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r10.anchor: وقال مقاتل: كان ابن عم فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r11.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r11.claim: Another group says he was an Israelite, with the phrase reordered to mean a man concealing his faith who was from Pharaoh’s people.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r11.anchor: وقالت فرقة: لم يكن من أهل فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r12.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers the first account because an Israelite could not have spoken this way before Pharaoh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r12.anchor: والأول أصح، ولم يكن لأحد من بني إسرائيل أن يتكلم بمثل هذا عند فرعون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r13.claim: He also allows that the man was not a Copt but counted among Pharaoh’s people because he outwardly followed Pharaoh’s religion and adherents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p555#2/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون من غير القبط، ويقال فيه من آل فرعون، إذ كان في الظاهر على دينه ومن أتباعه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r1.claim: Aʿraka al-Thaqafi’s elegy uses “the house of Abu Bakr” for Muslims who followed Abu Bakr, illustrating that affiliation can mean adherents.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r1.anchor: فلا تبك ميتا بعد ميت أجنه ... علي وعباس وآل أبي بكر يعني المسلمين إذ كانوا في طاعة أبي بكر الصديق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r2.claim: The phrase an yaqūla is a purpose complement: they would kill the man because he says “My Lord is God.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r2.anchor: وقوله: أن يقول مفعول من أجله، أي لأجل أن يقول

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r3.claim: The believer joins Pharaoh’s debate, then turns its uncertainty to his advantage by allowing either possibility and presenting his warning as counsel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r3.anchor: وجلّح معهم هذا المؤمن في هذه المقالات ثم غالطهم بعد في أن جعله في احتمال الصدق والكذب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r4.speaker: سيبويه؛ المبرد؛ أبو علي الفارسي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r4.claim: They offer different accounts of the dropped nūn in yak: Sibawayh treats it as lightening; al-Mubarrad compares it to the nūn of second-person plurals and duals; Abu Ali compares it to final weak letters after jussive marking.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r4.anchor: وحذفت النون من: يك تخفيفا على ما قال سيبويه وتشبيها بالنون في تفعلون وتفعلان على مذهب المبرد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r5.speaker: أبو عبيدة وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r5.claim: Abu Ubayda and others take baʿḍ as “all” and cite al-Qutami’s verse as evidence.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r5.anchor: فقال أبو عبيدة وغيره: بعض بمعنى كل، وأنشدوا قول القطامي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r6.speaker: القطامي عمرو بن شييم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r6.claim: Al-Qutami’s line is cited in support of interpreting “some” as “all.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r6.anchor: قول القطامي عمرو بن شييم: [البسيط] قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته ... وقد يكون مع المستعجل الزلل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the wording establishes the proof through the least that could happen, without denying that all of it may happen.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r7.anchor: وقال الزجاج: هو إلزام الحجة بأيسر ما في الأمر، وليس فيه نفي إضافة الكل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r8.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r8.claim: One group means some of the promised torment, which by itself would suffice to destroy them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r8.anchor: وقالت فرقة، أراد: يصبكم بعض العذاب الذي يذكر، وذلك كاف في هلاككم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r9.claim: Ibn Atiyya reads it as one part of the promise: Moses promised reward for belief and punishment for unbelief, so punishment is one part of what he promised.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r9.anchor: ويظهر إلي أن المعنى: يصبكم القسم الواحد مما يعد به، وذلك هو بعض ما يعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r10.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r10.claim: Another group takes “some” as the punishment of this world, one portion of the punishment in the afterlife; even that portion suffices to destroy them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r10.anchor: وقالت فرقة: أراد ببعض ما يعدكم عذاب الدنيا، لأنه بعض عذاب الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r11.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r11.claim: Al-Suddi says the profligacy is excessive killing.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r12.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p556/r12.claim: Qatada says the profligacy is unbelief.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r1.claim: As Pharaoh sought to kill Moses, the believing man from Pharaoh's people spoke up.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r1.anchor: فقصد فرعون قتل موسى فقال حينئذ ﴿ رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون ﴾

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r2.speaker: السدي ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r2.claim: One meaning of āl is family and lineage; al-Suddi and Muqatil say the believer was Pharaoh's cousin, identified with the man at 28:20.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r2.anchor: أحدهما أنه بمعنى الأهل والنسب قال السدي ومقاتل كان ابن عم فرعون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r3.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r3.claim: A second meaning of āl is tribe or clan; Qatada and Muqatil say he was a Copt.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r3.anchor: والثاني أنه بمعنى القبيلة والعشيرة قال قتادة ومقاتل كان قبطيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r4.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r4.claim: Some say he was an Israelite and that “from Pharaoh's people” means he concealed his faith among them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r4.anchor: وقال قوم كان إسرائيليا وإنما المعنى قال رجل مؤمن يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r5.speaker: ابن عباس ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas and Muqatil give the believer's name as Hizbil.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r5.anchor: أحدها حزبيل قاله ابن عباس ومقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r6.speaker: كعب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r6.claim: Kaʿb gives the believer's name as Habib.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r7.speaker: شعيب الجبائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r7.claim: Shuʿayb al-Jubbaʾi gives the name as Samiʿun, with the letter sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r7.anchor: والثالث سمعون بالسين المهملة قاله شعيب الجبائي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r8.claim: A fourth transmitted name is Jibril.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r8.anchor: والرابع جبريل والخامس شمعان بالشين المعجمة رويا عن ابن إسحاق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r9.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r9.claim: Ibn Ishaq transmits the name Shamʿan with shin; al-Zajjaj and Ibn Makula also report this spelling.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r9.anchor: والخامس شمعان بالشين المعجمة رويا عن ابن إسحاق وكذلك حكى الزجاج شمعان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r10.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r10.claim: Most commentators say the man believed in Moses when Moses came.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r10.anchor: والأكثرون على أنه آمن بموسى لما جاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r11.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r11.claim: Al-Hasan says the man believed before Moses came, as did Pharaoh's wife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r11.anchor: وقال الحسن كان مؤمنا قبل مجيء موسى وكذلك امرأة فرعون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r12.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r12.claim: Muqatil says the believer concealed his faith from Pharaoh for one hundred years.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r12.anchor: قال مقاتل كتم إيمانه من فرعون مائة سنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r13.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r13.claim: The phrase means “because he says, ‘My Lord is God’” and is a rebuking rhetorical question.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r13.anchor: ﴿ أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ﴾ أي لأن يقول ﴿ ربي الله ﴾ وهذا استفهام إنكار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r14.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r14.claim: The clear proofs are signs demonstrating Moses' truthfulness.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r15.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r15.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r15.claim: If Moses lies, the lie harms him alone and does not harm them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r16.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r16.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r16.claim: Abu ʿUbayda says baʿḍ can mean “all,” adducing a line by Labid in which “some souls” means all souls.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r16.anchor: أحدها أنها بمعنى كل قاله أبو عبيدة وأنشد للبيد تراك أمكنة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r17.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r17.speaker: الليث
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r17.claim: Al-Layth says baʿḍ is an expletive here, so the sense is that what Moses threatens will befall them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r17.anchor: والثاني أنها صلة والمعنى يصبكم الذي يعدكم حكي عن الليث

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r18.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r18.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r18.claim: Al-Mawardi preserves the literal “some”: the warning covers either rescue for belief or destruction for disbelief, so one outcome is only part of the alternatives.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r18.anchor: أحدهما أنه وعدهم النجاة إن آمنوا والهلاك إن كفروا فدخل ذكر البعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r19.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r19.speaker: الماوردي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r19.claim: Al-Mawardi's other explanation is that worldly destruction is only part of the promised punishment, which also includes the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r19.anchor: والثاني أنه وعدهم على كفرهم الهلاك في الدنيا والعذاب في الآخرة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r20.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r20.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r20.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the believer argues from the least concession, which establishes his case without denying that the full threat may occur.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r20.anchor: قال الزجاج هذا باب من النظر يذهب فيه المناظر إلى إلزام الحجة بأيسر ما في الأمر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r21.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r21.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r21.claim: The proverb about a patient person attaining some need while a hasty person may err shows the force of an opponent-proof minimum claim.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p216#3/r21.anchor: ومثله قول الشاعر قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته وقد يكون من المستعجل الزلل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that mentioning a part entails the whole because a part belongs to the whole; conceding only that some threat will come still establishes danger.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r1.anchor: وإنما ذكر البعض ليوجب الكل لأن البعض من الكل ولكن القائل إذا قال أقل ما يكون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r2.claim: In Labid's cited verse, “some souls” means the poet himself alone.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r2.anchor: قال وأما بيت لبيد فإنه أراد ببعض النفوس نفسه وحدها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r3.claim: “God does not guide” means He does not grant right judgment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r3.anchor: قوله تعالى ﴿ إن الله لا يهدي ﴾ أي لا يوفق للصواب ﴿ من هو مسرف ﴾ وفيه قولان

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r4.claim: Qatada takes “profligate” to mean a polytheist.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r4.anchor: وفيه قولان أحدهما أنه المشرك قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r5.claim: Mujahid takes “profligate” to mean one who sheds blood.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p218/r5.anchor: والثاني أنه السفاك للدم قاله مجاهد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r1.claim: The well-known view is that the believing man was a Copt from Pharaoh's household.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r1.anchor: المشهور أن هذا الرجل المؤمن كان قبطيا من آل فرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r2.claim: Al-Suddī says the believing man was Pharaoh's cousin.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r2.anchor: قال السدي: كان ابن عم فرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r3.speaker: قيل
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r3.claim: An unspecified view identifies the believing man as the person who escaped with Moses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r3.anchor: ويقال: إنه الذي نجا مع موسى

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r4.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r4.claim: Ibn Jarīr preferred that the man was a Copt from Pharaoh's family and rejected the Israelite identification, since Pharaoh listened to him and stopped short of killing Moses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r4.anchor: واختاره ابن جرير (2) ، ورد قول من ذهب إلى أنه كان إسرائيليا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says only this man, Pharaoh's wife, and the person who warned Moses that the chiefs planned to kill him believed among Pharaoh's household; Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmitted it via Ibn Jurayj.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r5.anchor: وقال ابن جريج عن ابن عباس: لم يؤمن من آل فرعون سوى هذا الرجل وامرأة فرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r6.claim: The man had concealed his faith from the Copts, then openly rebuked Pharaoh out of anger for God; the commentator calls this a just word before an unjust ruler, the greatest such word before Pharaoh.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r6.anchor: فأخذت الرجل غضبة لله عز وجل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr recounts that ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ strangled the praying Prophet at the Kaʿbah until Abū Bakr pulled him away and recited this verse; al-Bukhārī alone reports it from al-Awzāʿī, with Ibn Isḥāq also transmitting it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r7.anchor: قلت لعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: أخبرني بأشد شيء مما صنعه المشركون برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r8.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r8.claim: ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ recounts Quraysh grabbing the Prophet's clothes after he challenged their worship of their ancestors; Abū Bakr held and defended him while crying and reciting the verse through its end. Ibn Abī Ḥātim transmits it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p140/r8.anchor: عن عمرو بن العاص أنه سئل: ما أشد ما رأيت قريشا بلغوا من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r1.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r1.claim: Al-Nasāʾī also reports the account through ʿAbdah, transmitting it as a report from ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r1.anchor: وهكذا رواه النسائي من حديث عبدة، فجعله من مسند عمرو بن العاص

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r2.claim: The believer reasons that Moses has brought proof, then argues that even if he is a liar, leaving him alone lets God punish him; if he is truthful, harming him risks some of the promised punishment, so restraint is prudent.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r2.anchor: فمن العقل والرأي التام والحزم أن تتركوه ونفسه، فلا تؤذوه، فإن يك كاذبا فإن الله سيجازيه على كذبه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r3.claim: The believer's plea for restraint resembles Moses asking Pharaoh's people for a truce and permission to preach; Moses says to leave him alone if they will not believe.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r3.anchor: عن موسى، عليه السلام، أنه طلب من فرعون وقومه الموادعة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r4.claim: The Prophet similarly asked Quraysh not to harm him and to preserve their kinship; Ibn Kathīr reads the request as enabling him to call people and connects it to the Hudaybiyyah truce and its clear victory.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141/r4.anchor: فلا تؤذوني وتتركوا بيني وبين الناس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141#2/r1.claim: If Moses were the liar they claim, his speech and actions would be plainly disordered; instead his course is sound, and God would not guide a profligate liar to such orderly conduct.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p141#2/r1.anchor: وهذا نرى أمره سديدا ومنهجه مستقيما، ولو كان من المسرفين الكذابين لما هداه الله، وأرشده إلى ما ترون من انتظام أمره وفعله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r1.claim: Ibn Masud called Ibn Abbas an excellent interpreter of the Quran; Ibn Kathir says the report's chain to Ibn Masud is sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r1.anchor: فهذا إسناد صحيح إلى ابن مسعود: أنه قال عن ابن عباس هذه العبارة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas outlived Ibn Masud by thirty-six years, so Ibn Kathir asks the reader to consider how much knowledge he gained afterward.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r2.anchor: وقد مات ابن مسعود، رضي الله عنه، في سنة اثنتين وثلاثين على الصحيح، وعمر بعده ابن عباس ستا وثلاثين سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r3.claim: After Ali appointed him to lead the pilgrimage, Ibn Abbas preached and explained al-Baqara, or al-Nur in another version, so powerfully that Romans, Turks, and Daylamites would have converted if they heard him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r3.anchor: وقال الأعمش عن أبي وائل: استخلف علي عبد الله بن عباس على الموسم، فخطب الناس، فقرأ

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r4.claim: Al-Suddi's tafsir mostly transmits from Ibn Masud and Ibn Abbas; sometimes their reports include Israelite material, which the Prophet permitted narrating so long as no one lies about him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r4.anchor: ولهذا غالب ما يرويه إسماعيل بن عبد الرحمن السدي الكبير في تفسيره، عن هذين الرجلين: عبد الله بن مسعود وابن عباس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r5.claim: Ibn Amr acquired two bundles of People of the Book's writings at Yarmuk and narrated from them, relying on the Prophet's permission to relate Israelite reports.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r5.anchor: ولهذا كان عبد الله بن عمرو يوم اليرموك قد أصاب زاملتين من كتب أهل الكتاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r6.claim: Ibn Kathir divides Israelite reports into three classes; the first is confirmed by Islamic evidence and is true, while the second is contradicted by Islamic evidence and is false.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p8/r6.anchor: أحدها: ما علمنا صحته مما بأيدينا مما يشهد له بالصدق، فذاك صحيح

JISHUMI:v1p685/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r1.claim: God hears and sees because He is living and without defect.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r1.anchor: وتدل على أنه سميع بصير؛ لأنه حي لا آفة به.

JISHUMI:v1p685/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r2.claim: His creation of bodies proves He is neither body nor accident, has no likeness, and is not in a place or substrate.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r2.anchor: ويدل خلقه الأجسام على أنه ليس بجسم ولا عرض؛ لأن خلق الجسم لا يصح منها

JISHUMI:v1p685/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r3.claim: Visibility belongs to bodies and accidents; God is independent because need belongs to bodies.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r3.anchor: لأن جواز الرؤية من صفات الأجسام والأعراض وأنه غني؛ لأن الحاجة من صفات الأجسام

JISHUMI:v1p685/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r4.claim: Since God is not a body, bodily organs such as hand and face cannot be affirmed of Him.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r4.anchor: وإذا ثبت أنه ليس بجسم لا يجوز إثبات اليد والوجه ونحوه من الأعضاء؛ لأنه من صفات الأجسام

JISHUMI:v1p685/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r5.claim: God is not a locus for accidents because He is not spatially extended; otherwise all accidents could inhere in Him.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r5.anchor: ويعلم أنه ليس بمحل للحوادث؛ لأنه ليس بمتحيز؛ ولأنه لو صح حلول بعضها صح حلول سائرها

JISHUMI:v1p685/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r6.claim: God differs from bodies and accidents through being eternal, so no other eternal being can accompany Him.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r6.anchor: وتدل على أنه مخالف للأجسام والأعراض، ولا بد من صفة بها خالف وهو كونه قديما

JISHUMI:v1p685/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r7.claim: God knows, has power, lives, and is eternal through His essence, not through added attributes.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r7.anchor: فعند ذلك يعلم أنه عالم لذاته، قادر لذاته، حي لذاته، قديم لذاته لا لمعان قديمة

JISHUMI:v1p685/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r8.claim: The Qurʾān is God's originated speech, not an eternal entity.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r8.anchor: ويعلم أن القرآن ليس بقديم، وأنه كلامه أحدثه

JISHUMI:v1p685/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r9.claim: God is one, since a second or third deity would allow mutual obstruction.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r9.anchor: وتدل على أنه واحد؛ إذ لو جاز إثبات ثان وثالث لصح التمانع

JISHUMI:v1p685/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r10.claim: Knowing evil's ugliness and having no need of it, God neither does nor wills evil.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r10.anchor: وإذا ثبت بأفعاله أنه عالم لذاته غني ثبت أنه لا يفعل القبيح؛ لأن العالم بقبح القبيح

JISHUMI:v1p685/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r11.claim: Human acts are not created by God because they include disbelief and other evils.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r11.anchor: وأن أفعال العباد ليست بخلق لله [*] لما فيها من الكفر والقبائح

JISHUMI:v1p685/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r12.claim: God charges people for their benefit, creates no one for punishment, and does not impose the impossible; capacity precedes action.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r12.anchor: وأنه كلف العباد لمنافعهم، ولم يخلق أحدا للعذاب لما فيه من القبح، وأنه يزيح العلة

JISHUMI:v1p685/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r13.claim: If God intends the obligated person to act and deserve reward, He must provide لطف, which is therefore obligatory.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r13.anchor: وإذا كان غرضه حصول الفعل من المكلف يستحق الثواب، فلا بد أن يلطف فيعلم وجوب اللطف

JISHUMI:v1p685/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r14.claim: God's freedom from evil entails His truthfulness and the validity of His promise and threat.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r14.anchor: وإذا علم أنه لا يجوز عليه القبائح يعلم كونه صادقا، فيعلم صحة ما جاء به الوعد والوعيد

JISHUMI:v1p685/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p685/r15.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p685/r15.claim: Because some لطف may come through human acts, messengers are necessary, with miracles, protection from sin, and knowledge of law as conditions.
JISHUMI:v1p685/r15.anchor: فلا بد من رسول يبين، فعند ذلك يعلم وجوب النبوات وشرائطها من المعجز والعصمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r1.claim: A variant reads رجل with a vowelless jīm, as in عضد.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r1.anchor: وقرىء : ( رجل ) بسكون الجيم كما يقال : عضد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r2.claim: One account makes the believer a Copt and Pharaoh’s cousin who secretly believed in Moses; another says he was an Israelite. The author favors Pharaoh’s kin, since Israelite believers were not few or weak.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r2.anchor: وكان قبطيا ابن عم لفرعون : آمن بموسى سرا وقيل : كان إسرائيليا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r3.claim: His name is given variously as Samʿān, Ḥabīb, or Ḥizbīl; the source also repeats the last form.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r3.anchor: واسمه سمعان أو حبيب وقيل حزبيل أو حزبيل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r4.claim: The phrase may describe the man or attach to يكتم, meaning that he concealed his faith from Pharaoh’s family.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r4.anchor: صفة لرجل . أو صلة ليكتم ، أي : يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r5.claim: The author cites Pharaoh’s own words at 40:25 and the believer’s warning at 40:29 as evidence that the believer addresses his own people with counsel.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r5.anchor: والدليل عليه قول فرعون : { فلما جاءهم بالحق من }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r6.claim: أن يقول means because he says; alternatively, a noun for time is understood, meaning at the moment he said it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r6.anchor: لأن يقول ، وهذا إنكار منه عظيم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r7.claim: The question forcefully condemns the atrocious killing of an inviolate person for no reason but his truthful confession; the believer also reminds them that the God he names is their Lord too, softening their fury.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r7.anchor: وهذا إنكار منه عظيم وتبكيت شديد ، كأنه قال : أترتكبون الفعلة الشنعاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r8.claim: Moses had brought multiple mighty signs from the one he calls Lord, who is not only his Lord but theirs; the reminder draws them toward acknowledging Him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r8.anchor: ولكن بينات عدة من عند من نسب إليه الربوبية ، وهو ربكم لا ربه وحده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r9.claim: The signs are the great clear proofs that the audience had known and witnessed.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r9.anchor: يريد : بالبينات العظيمة التي عهدتموها وشهدتموها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r10.claim: The believer sets up a dilemma: if Moses lies, the harm of his lie stays with him; if he is truthful, some promised harm will reach them if they attack him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r10.anchor: ثم أخذهم بالاحتجاج على طريقة التقسيم فقال : لا يخلو من أن يكون كاذبا أو صادقا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r11.claim: Though a truthful prophet’s full warning must come to pass, the speaker says only some to conciliate Moses’ opponents and sound fair, increasing the chance they will listen and accept his point.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r11.anchor: لأنه احتاج في مقاولة خصوم موسى ومنا كريه إلى أن يلاوصهم ويداريهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r12.claim: By granting only part on the surface, the believer appears to understate Moses’ claim rather than defend him, although his premise that Moses is truthful entails the whole warning; putting the liar first serves the same tact.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r12.anchor: فقد أثبت أنه صادق في جميع ما يعد ، ولكنه أردفه { يصبكم بعض الذى يعدكم }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r13.claim: The closing claim that God does not guide a profligate liar follows the same tactful, apparently even-handed argument.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r13.anchor: وكذلك قوله : { إن الله * يهدى من هو مسرف كذاب }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r14.speaker: أبو عبيدة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r14.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets بعض as meaning all and cites a line by Labīd as evidence; its text is not included in this segment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p166#2/r14.anchor: فعن أبي عبيدة أنه فسر البعض بالكل ، وأنشد بيت لبيد :

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r1.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r1.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the believer as Pharaoh's cousin and says he was the one who escaped with Moses.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r1.anchor: فيه قولان : أحدهما : أنه كان ابن عم فرعون , قاله السدي , قال وهو الذي نجا مع موسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r2.claim: Muqatil says the man was a Copt of Pharaoh's ethnicity, but not a member of his family.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r2.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان قبطيا من جنسه ولم يكن من أهله , قاله مقاتل .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r3.claim: Ibn Ishaq gives the believer's name as Habib.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r3.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق : وكان أسمه حبيب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r4.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r4.claim: Al-Kalbi calls him Hizbil and says he ruled half the people, as crown prince after Pharaoh.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r4.anchor: وحكى الكلبي أن اسمه حزبيل , وكان ملكا على نصف الناس وله الملك بعد فرعون , بمنزلة ولي العهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh's family had no believer besides this man and Pharaoh's wife, and mentions the man who warned Moses at 28:20.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : لم يكن من آل فرعون مؤمن غيره وامرأة فرعون وغير المؤمن الذي أنذر فقال ^ { إن الملأ يأتمرون بك } ^

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r6.claim: One view is that he believed when Moses arrived and affirmed his message; Mawardi calls this the apparent reading.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r6.anchor: وفي إيمانه قولان : أحدهما : أنه آمن بمجيء موسى وتصديقه له وهو الظاهر .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r7.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r7.claim: Al-Hasan says the man, like Pharaoh's wife, was already a believer before Moses came.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r7.anchor: الثاني : أنه كان مؤمنا قبل مجيء موسى وكذلك امرأة فرعون قاله الحسن , فكتم إيمانه

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r8.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak says he concealed faith to deal gently with his people, then declared it while speaking in a concealed state.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r8.anchor: قال الضحاك كان يكتم إيمانه للرفق بقومه ثم أظهره فقال ذلك في حال كتمه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r9.claim: The question means: would you kill a man merely for saying, “My Lord is God”?
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r9.anchor: أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربي الله } أي لقوله ربي الله .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r10.speaker: السدي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r10.claim: Al-Suddi explains the clear proofs as the lawful and unlawful rulings Moses brought.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r10.anchor: فيها قولان : أحدهما : أنه الحلال والحرام , قاله السدي .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r11.speaker: يحيى
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r11.claim: Yahya identifies the proofs as Moses' signs, including his hand, staff, and the flood, linking to 7:130.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r11.anchor: الثاني : أنها الآيات التي جاءتهم : يده وعصاه والطوفان وغيرها , كما قال تعالى ^ { ولقد أخذنا آل فرعون بالسنين ونقص من الثمرات } ^

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r12.claim: The believer does not doubt Moses' truth; he tactfully urges the people to refrain from harming him.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r12.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك لشك منه في رسالته وصدقه ولكن تلطفا في الاستكفاف واستنزالا عن الأذى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r13.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r13.claim: Moses promised rescue for belief and destruction for disbelief; either outcome would fulfill only part of the promise.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r13.anchor: أحدها : أنه كان وعدهم بالنجاة إن آمنوا وبالهلاك إن كفروا , فقال { يصبكم بعض الذي يعدكم }

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r14.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r14.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r14.claim: A second explanation is that worldly destruction is only part of the threatened punishment, which also includes the afterlife.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r14.anchor: الثاني : لأنه قد كان أوعدهم على كفرهم بالهلاك في الدنيا والعذاب في الآخرة , فصار هلاكهم في الدنيا بعض وما وعدهم

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r15.claim: A third explanation is that the first punishment is only the beginning of successive stages, while the rest will then be certain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p152/r15.anchor: الثالث : أن الذي يبدؤهم من العذاب هو أوله ثم يتوالى عليهم حالا بعد حال حتى يستكمل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r1.claim: “Some” can tactfully mean the whole; the unnamed poet's line illustrates this broad usage.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r1.anchor: قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته … وقد يكون مع المستعجل الزلل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r2.claim: One reading points to Moses: excessive against himself and lying about his Lord; these are the believer's words.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r2.anchor: أحدهما : مسرف على نفسه كذاب على ربه إشارة إلى موسى , ويكون هذا من قول المؤمن .

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r3.claim: Another reading points to Pharaoh, excessive in stubbornness and lying in his claim; the words are God's narration.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p153/r3.anchor: الثاني : مسرف في عناده كذاب في ادعائه إشارة إلى فرعون [ ويكون ] هذا من قوله تعالى .

MUQATIL:40:25-28/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r8.claim: The believing man was a Copt like Pharaoh and had concealed his faith for one hundred years, until Pharaoh spoke of killing Moses.
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r8.anchor: { وقال رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون } يعنى قبطى مثل فرعون { يكتم إيمانه } مائة سنة حتى سمع قول فرعون

MUQATIL:40:25-28/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r9.speaker: رجل مؤمن من آل فرعون
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r9.claim: The believer argues that Moses came with the signs of hand and staff; if he lies, his lie harms him, but if truthful, some promised punishment will strike them.
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r9.anchor: فقال المؤمن: { أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربى الله وقد جاءكم بالبينات من ربكم } يعنى اليد والعصا { وإن يك } موسى { كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا

MUQATIL:40:25-28/r10.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r10.speaker: author
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r10.claim: The extravagant liar whom God does not guide is a polytheist and fabricator.
MUQATIL:40:25-28/r10.anchor: { إن الله لا يهدي } إلى دينه { من هو مسرف كذاب } [آية: 28] يعنى مشرك مفتن

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r1.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r1.claim: One account makes the believer a Copt and Pharaoh's cousin who secretly believed in Moses; Nasafi says this first account is the apparent one.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r1.anchor: قيل كان قبطيا ابن عم لفرعون امن بموسى سرا ومن ال فرعون صفة لرجل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r2.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r2.claim: Another account makes him an Israelite, with “from Pharaoh's people” modifying “concealing his faith,” meaning he hid it from Pharaoh's family; he is variously named Samʿān, Ḥabīb, Khirbīl or Ḥizbīl.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r2.anchor: وقيل كان اسرائيليا من آل فرعون صلة ليكتم اى يكتم ايمانه من ال فرعون واسمه سمعان أو حبيب أو خربيل أو حزبيل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r3.claim: The phrase means “because he says”; the believer condemns killing a protected person when the only alleged offense is speaking the truth that Allah is his Lord—and theirs too.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r3.anchor: لان يقول وهذا انكار منه عظيم كانه قيل اترتكبون الفعلة الشنعاء التي هي قتل نفس محرمة ومالكم علة في ارتكابها الا كلمة الحق

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r4.claim: “And he has brought you” is a circumstantial clause; the believer stresses that Moses came with multiple proofs from the one to whom he attributes lordship, leading them toward acknowledgment.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r4.anchor: يعني انه لم يحضر لتصحيح قوله ببينة واحدة ولكن ببينات من عند من اسب اليه الربوبية

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r5.claim: The believer argues by exhaustive division: if Moses lies, the harm and burden of his lie fall on him alone.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r5.anchor: احتج عليهم بطريق التقسيم فانه لا يخلو من ان يكون كاذبا أو صادقا فان يك كاذبا فعليه وبال كذبه ولا يتخطاه

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r6.claim: If Moses is truthful, some of the threatened punishment will reach them; saying “some” rather than “all” is diplomatic fairness designed to make acceptance easier, without denying that all might happen.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r6.anchor: ولم يقل كل الذى يعدكم مع انه وعد من نبي صادق القول مداراة لهم وسلوكا لطريق الانصاف فجاء بما هو اقرب إلى تسليمهم له وليس فيه نفى اصابه الكل

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r7.claim: Nasafi rejects interpreting “some” as “all”; rather, it may be the immediate worldly punishment, while Moses had promised punishment in this world and the next.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r7.anchor: لعل ما يكون في صدقه ان يصيبكم بعض ما يعدكم وهو العذاب العاجل وفى ذلك هلاككم وكان وعدهم عذاب الدنيا والاخرة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r8.claim: Putting the liar's case before the truthful one's is another instance of tactful persuasion.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r8.anchor: الكاذب على الصادق من هذا القبيل ايضا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r9.claim: An extravagant person has exceeded the proper limit; “liar” here means one making a false claim.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r10.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r10.claim: The believer may be speaking diplomatically: an extravagant liar would be abandoned and destroyed by Allah, freeing the people from him; or Allah would not grant him prophethood and support him with proofs.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r10.anchor: وهذا ايضا من باب المجاملة والمعنى انه كان مسرفا كذابا خذله الله واهلكه فتتخلصون منه أو لو كان مسرفا كذابا لما هداه الله بالنبوة

NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r11.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r11.claim: An alternative says he insinuated that Moses was meant by “extravagant liar,” while intending Pharaoh.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p72#3/r11.anchor: وقيل اوهم انه عنى بالمسرف موسى وهو يعنى به فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r1.claim: Some commentators identify the believer as Habib.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r1.anchor: ذكر بعض المفسرين: أن اسم هذا الرجل حبيب

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r2.speaker: السهيلي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r2.claim: Al-Suhayli considers Shimaʿan, with dotted shin, the strongest reported name.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r2.anchor: قال السهيلي: وهو أصح ما قيل فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r3.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r3.claim: Al-Tabari's History gives his name as Khabarak.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r3.anchor: وفي تاريخ الطبري رحمه الله: اسمه خبرك

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r4.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi transmits from Ibn Abbas and most scholars that his name was Hizqil.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r4.anchor: ذكره الثعلبي عن ابن عباس وأكثر العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari gives Simʿan or Habib as names, and also reports Khurbil or Hizbil.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r6.speaker: الحسن وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r6.claim: Al-Hasan and others say the believer was a Copt; al-Suddi says he was Pharaoh's cousin and escaped with Moses.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r7.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says he was Pharaoh's cousin and the man who escaped with Moses, explaining why he is called one of Pharaoh's people.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r7.anchor: قاله السدي. قال: وهو الذي نجا مع موسى عليه السلام

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r8.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r8.claim: Muqatil identifies him with the man who came running from the farthest part of the city to warn Moses at 28:20.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r8.anchor: وهذا الرجل هو المراد بقوله تعالى:

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says Pharaoh's household had no believer besides this man, Pharaoh's wife, and the believer who warned Moses that the council planned to kill him.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لم يكن من آل فرعون مؤمن غيره

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r10.claim: A prophetic report calls three people ṣiddiqūn: Habib of Ya-Sin, Pharaoh's believer, and Abu Bakr, the best of them.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r10.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r11.claim: The report consoles the Prophet: he should not be surprised by the polytheists among his own people.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r11.anchor: وفي هذا تسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أي لا تعجب من مشركي قومك

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r12.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r12.claim: The believer's standing with Pharaoh explains why Pharaoh did not harm him.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r12.anchor: وكان هذا الرجل له وجاهة عند فرعون فلهذا لم يتعرض له بسوء

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r13.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r13.claim: Another report from al-Suddi makes the believer an Israelite who concealed his faith from Pharaoh's people, requiring fronted-and-delayed word order.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r13.anchor: يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون عن السدي أيضا

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r14.claim: If he was Coptic, min describes his affiliation as a member or relative of Pharaoh's household; if Israelite, it attaches to yaktum as the second object.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r14.anchor: فمن جعل الرجل قبطيا ف«من» عنده متعلقة بمحذوف

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r15.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r15.claim: Al-Qushayri objects to the Israelite reading: Arabic says conceal something, not conceal it from someone in this construction, and Pharaoh would not tolerate it.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r15.anchor: القشيري: ومن جعله إسرائيليا ففيه بعد لأنه يقال

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r16.claim: An here means because: it is accusative after deletion of a governing preposition.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r16.anchor: أي لأن يقول ومن أجل «أن يقول ربي الله»

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r17.claim: The clear signs that came with Moses are the nine signs.

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r18.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r18.claim: The believer did not doubt Moses's message or truthfulness; he spoke tactfully to restrain them from harming Moses.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r18.anchor: ولم يكن ذلك لشك منه في رسالته وصدقه، ولكن تلطفا

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r19.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r19.claim: Sibawayh explains the dropped n in yakun as due to frequent use; al-Abbas instead treats it as the inflectional n.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r19.anchor: ولكن حذفت النون لكثرة الاستعمال على قول سيبويه

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r20.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r20.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r20.claim: Abu Ubayda says baʿḍ can mean all: if any threatened punishment reaches them, the full threat encompasses them; this softens admonition.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28/r20.anchor: ومذهب أبي عبيدة أن معنى «بعض الذي يعدكم» كل الذي يعدكم

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r1.speaker: لبيد
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r1.claim: Labid's line uses baʿḍ in the sense of all, offered as evidence for Abu Ubayda's interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r1.anchor: تراك أمكنة إذا لم أرضها أو يرتبط بعض النفوس حمامها

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r2.speaker: الماوردي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r2.claim: Al-Mawardi says baʿḍ may stand for all as tactful, expansive speech; he cites a line about patience attaining some wishes and haste leading to error.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r2.anchor: وذكر الماوردي: أن البعض قد يستعمل في موضع الكل تلطفا في الخطاب وتوسعا في الكلام كما قال الشاعر: قد يدرك المتأني بعض حاجته

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r3.claim: One view says Moses warned of several kinds of torment, each deadly, so suffering any part meant a fatal threat.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r3.anchor: وقيل أيضا: قال ذلك لأنه حذرهم أنواعا من العذاب كل نوع منها مهلك

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r4.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r4.claim: Another view says Moses threatened worldly or afterlife punishment for disbelief, so the phrase means one of the two punishments would reach them.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r4.anchor: وقيل: وعدهم موسى بعذاب الدنيا أو بعذاب الآخرة إن كفروا

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r5.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r5.claim: Another explanation takes the phrase as some warning fulfilled in this world, with more punishment following in the afterlife.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r5.anchor: وقيل: أي يصبكم هذا العذاب الذي يقوله في الدنيا وهو بعض الوعيد

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r6.claim: A further view says Moses promised punishment for disbelief and reward for belief; by disbelieving, they would incur part of what he promised.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: وعدهم العذاب إن كفروا والثواب إن آمنوا

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r7.speaker: المؤمن
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r7.claim: If the believer speaks these words, the wasteful one is Moses's opponent to himself and a liar against his Lord.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r7.anchor: إشارة إلى موسى ويكون هذا من قول المؤمن

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r8.speaker: الله تعالى
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, God speaks here about Pharaoh, wasteful in obstinacy and lying in his claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: «مسرف» في عناده «كذاب» في ادعائه إشارة إلى فرعون

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r9.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r9.claim: Ibn al-Arabi reports that some wrongly infer a person who hides faith without verbalizing it is not a believer by conviction; he then qualifies the claim.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r9.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر بن العربي: ظن بعضهم أن المكلف

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r10.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r10.claim: Malik's analogy is that a husband's inward intention to divorce his wife takes effect, just as belief and disbelief may reside in the heart.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r10.anchor: وقد قال مالك: إن الرجل إذا نوى بقلبه طلاق زوجته

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r11.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r11.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says intending disbelief makes one an unbeliever without speech, but intending faith alone never makes one a believer until it is professed.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r11.anchor: أن المكلف إذا نوى الكفر بقلبه كان كافرا وإن لم يتلفظ

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r12.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r12.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says fear or dissimulation may prevent others hearing a profession, but cannot excuse omitting it before God; public hearing protects life and property, not validity.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r12.anchor: ولا تمنعه التقية والخوف من أن يتلفظ بلسانه

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r13.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r13.claim: In a report in al-Bukhari and Muslim, Uqba ibn Abi Muʿayt strangled the Prophet at the Kaaba; Abu Bakr intervened and cited the verse in defense.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r13.anchor: روى البخاري ومسلم عن عروة بن الزبير قال: قلت لعبد الله

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r14.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r14.claim: Al-Tirmidhi al-Hakim's Nawadir al-Usul reports Ali saying Quraysh sought to kill the Prophet three days after Abu Talib's death; Abu Bakr defended him, shouting the verse and losing a braid.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#2/r14.anchor: خرجه الترمذي الحكيم في «نوادر الأصول» من حديث جعفر بن محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r1.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r1.claim: Ali says Abu Bakr's day was better than the Pharaoh believer's: the latter concealed faith, while Abu Bakr openly gave his faith, wealth, and life.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r1.anchor: فقال علي: والله ليوم أبي بكر خير من مؤمن آل فرعون إن ذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi limits Ali's remark to the believer's initial concealment: the Quran says he openly declared faith when Moses was threatened with death.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r2.anchor: قلت: قول علي رضي الله عنه إن ذلك رجل كتم إيمانه يريد في أول أمره

QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r3.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r3.claim: Asma reports Quraysh discussed the Prophet's words about idols, seized him in the mosque, and turned on Abu Bakr when he cited the verse; they pulled out his braids.
QURTUBI-FULL:40:28#3/r3.anchor: عن أسماء بنت أبي بكر رضي الله عنها قالوا لها: ما أشد شيء
